ITQAN:v4p345/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p345/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p345/r1.claim: As dross disappears when gold is put into fire, falsehood likewise vanishes from its adherents.
ITQAN:v4p345/r1.anchor: وكما اضمحل خبث هذا الذهب حين أدخل في النار كذلك يضمحل الباطل عن أهله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p549/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p549/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p549/r6.claim: Muqātil ibn Sulaymān interprets the water in the parable of 13:17 as the Qur'an, likening it to water that gives life; the source says he alone is reported to give this sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p549/r6.anchor: وهذا الوجه مذكور عن مقاتل بن سليمان . ويقال : إنه انفرد به

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The sūras address the conflict between truth and evil after the Qur'an's revelation and identify the group destined to prevail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: a conflict between truth and evil ensued when the Qur’ ān was revealed. This sūrahs highlights the group which was supposed to succeed ultimately in this conflict.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Yūsuf argues through events in Joseph's life, whereas al-Raʿd argues from human intellect and nature.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: in this sūrah, arguments are drawn from human intellect and nature for this purpose

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Verses 17–22 are identified as the sūra's thematic center.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Verses 17 to 22 highlight the theme of the sūrah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi rejects the codices' Madinan classification: in his view, the sūra is wholly Makkan, with no Madinan verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some codices regard it to be Madī nan, which I fail to understand. Not one of its verse is Mad īnan in my opinion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The signs illustrate that God preserves what benefits and removes what does not.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God keeps intact what is beneficial and destroys that is not.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: This image assures that God will uproot evil and make truth prevail in the conflict following the Qur'an's revelation and the Prophet's preaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God will root out evil and make the truth prevail.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r18.speaker: أبو الحجاج الأعلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r18.claim: Abū al-Ḥajjāj al-Aʿlam defines zabad as the foam cast off by a river when it swells and its waves churn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r18.anchor: قال أبو الحجاج الأعلم هو ما يطرحه الوادي إذا جاش ماؤه واضطربت أمواجه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r19.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya describes zabad as flood-borne scum and tangled bubbles thrown onto the banks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: هو ما يحمله السيل من غثاء ونحوه، وما يرمي به على ضفتيه من الحباب الملتبك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r20.speaker: ابن عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r20.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā defines zabad as the impurity or froth produced by boiling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r20.anchor: وقال ابن عيسى: الزبد وضر الغليان وخبثه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r21.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r21.claim: An unnamed poet's image of the Euphrates casting foam illustrates the word zabad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r21.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فما الفرات إذا هب الرياح له ... ترمي غواربه العبرين بالزبد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r1.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص، وابن محيصن، ومجاهد، وطلحة، ويحيى، وأهل الكوفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r1.claim: These readers have يوقدون with yāʾ, third-person plural: people kindle the fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص، وابن محيصن، ومجاهد، وطلحة، ويحيى، وأهل الكوفة: يوقدون بالياء على الغيبة، أي يوقد الناس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r2.speaker: باقي السبعة والحسن، وأبو جعفر، والأعرج، وشيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r2.claim: These readers have توقدون with tāʾ, addressing the audience as those who kindle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة والحسن، وأبو جعفر، والأعرج، وشيبة: بالتاء على الخطاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي، والحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī and al-Ḥawfī attach في النار to توقدون.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r3.anchor: وفي النار. قال أبو علي، والحوفي: متعلق بتوقدون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī notes that one can kindle something without placing it in a fire, as in the command to kindle clay; the fire’s flame merely reaches it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو علي: قد يوقد على كل شيء وليس في النار كقوله: فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فذلك البناء الذي أمر به يوقد عليه، وليس في النار، لكن يصيبه لهبها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r5.speaker: مكي وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r5.claim: Makkī and others attach في النار to an omitted state, such as being present or fixed there; they reject attachment to توقدون because kindling already entails fire and attachment would distinguish one condition from another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r5.anchor: وقال مكي وغيره: في النار متعلق بمحذوف تقديره: كائنا، أو ثابتا. ومنعوا تعليقه بقوله: توقدون، لأنهم زعموا أنه لا يوقد على شيء إلا وهو في النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān allows attachment to توقدون even if every kindled thing is in fire, treating the phrase as emphatic like يطير بجناحيه.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r6.anchor: ولو قلنا: إنه لا يوقد على شيء إلا وهو في النار، لجاز أن يكون متعلقا بتوقدون، ويجوز ذلك على سبيل التوكيد كما قالوا في قوله: يطير بجناحيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r7.claim: ابتغاء is accusative as a purpose object because it meets the conditions for that construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r7.anchor: وانتصب ابتغاء على أنه مفعول من أجله، وشروط المفعول من أجله موجودة فيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r8.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥawfī instead treats ابتغاء as a verbal noun used circumstantially, meaning those who seek adornment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r8.anchor: وقال الحوفي: هو مصدر في موضع الحال أي: مبتغين حلية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r9.claim: Mentioning the object of ابتغاء draws attention to the benefit of what is kindled: gold and silver adornments for women, and useful tools and goods made from iron, copper, and similar metals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r9.anchor: وفي ذكر متعلق ابتغاء تنبيه على منفعة ما يوقدون عليه. والحلية ما يعمل للنساء مما يتزين به من الذهب والفضة، والمتاع ما يتخذ من الحديد والنحاس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r10.claim: زبد is a subject whose predicate is ومما توقدون; مِن is partitive because the foam is part of the metals being kindled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r10.anchor: وزبد مرفوع بالابتداء، وخبره في قوله: ومما توقدون. ومن الظاهر أنها للتبعيض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r11.claim: Zamakhsharī allows مِن to mark origin: metal foam arises from the material, just as water foam arises from water, both from dirt and impurities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r11.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن تكون من لابتداء الغاية أي: ومنه ينشأ زبد مثل زبد الماء، والمماثلة في كونهما يتولدان من الأوساخ والأكدار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r12.claim: Truth and falsehood are understood with an omitted comparison: truth resembles purified metal, lasting and useful, while falsehood resembles foam and impurities, with no permanence or value.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r12.anchor: والحق والباطل على حذف مضاف أي: مثل الحق والباطل. شبه الحق بما يخلص من جرم هذه المعادن من الأقذار والخبث ودوام الانتفاع بها، وشبه الباطل بالزبد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r13.claim: The exposition begins with foam because it was mentioned last in the examples and falsehood is the later term; beginning with what was named first is also eloquent, sometimes foregrounding what matters most.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r13.anchor: وفصل ما سبق ذكره مما ينتفع به ومن الزبد، فبدأ بالزبد إذ هو المتأخر في قوله: زبدا رابيا، وفي قوله: زبد مثله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r14.claim: The convention of beginning with what was mentioned last is illustrated by the faces turning black before the faces turning white; starting with what was mentioned first is also eloquent and may foreground the more important item.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r14.anchor: وهي طريقة فصيحة يبدأ في التقسيم بما ذكر آخرا كقوله: يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r15.claim: جفاء is a circumstantial accusative meaning dissolved and vanished, with no use or permanence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r15.anchor: وانتصب جفاء على الحال أي: مضمحلا متلاشيا لا منفعة فيه ولا بقاء له.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r16.claim: Foam refers to both the flood’s residue and metal dross; it is singular because both share the property of being foam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r16.anchor: والزبد يراد به ما سبق من ما احتمله السيل وما خرج من حيث المعادن، وأفرد الزبد بالذكر ولم يثن، وإن تقدم زبدان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r17.speaker: رؤبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r17.claim: Ruʾba reads جفالا with lām instead of the hamza in جفاء.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p373#2/r17.anchor: وقرأ رؤبة: جفالا باللام بدل الهمزة من

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r1.claim: Ruʾba’s form is supported by the expression جفلت الريح السحاب, meaning the wind carried off and scattered the clouds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r1.anchor: قولهم: جفلت الريح السحاب إذا حملته وفرقته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r2.claim: Abū Ḥātim rejects Ruʾba’s reading, disparaging him as a crude Bedouin who ate mice, and also says Bedouin Quran readings should not be considered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r2.anchor: وعن أبي حاتم: لا يقرأ بقراءة رؤبة، لأنه كان يأكل الفأر بمعنى: أنه كان أعرابيا جافيا. وعن أبي حاتم أيضا: لا تعتبر قراءة الأعراب في القرآن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r3.claim: What benefits people is the clean water after scum separates and the pure metal after its dross separates; this exemplifies truth and falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p375/r3.anchor: وأما ما ينفع الناس أي: من الماء الخالص من الغثاء ومن الجوهر المعدني الخالص من الخبث أي: مثل ذلك الضرب كمثل الحق والباطل.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.claim: Al-Raʿd’s aim is to portray revelation as true in itself: sometimes its sound and fame move people toward guidance, while sometimes it instead leaves them blind and astray, like thunder whose lightning and rain may benefit, fail, or harm according to where they fall.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بأنه الحق في نفسه ، وتارة يتأثر عنه مع أن له صوتا وصيتا وإرعابا وإرهابا

STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r8.claim: A parable of water from the sky illustrates the sharp difference between truth and falsehood.
STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r8.anchor: an important parable of water from the sky is provided in order to illustrate

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.speaker: الشيخ الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.claim: Al-Ghazali likens the heart to an enclosure receiving states from many entrances and to a target struck by arrows from every side.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.anchor: الشيخ الغزالي في كتاب الإحياء قال : القلب مثل قبة لها أبواب تنصب إليها الأحوال من كل باب

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.claim: Razi's summary of al-Ghazali adds that the heart is a mirror reflecting passing forms and a basin receiving waters from different streams.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.anchor: أو مثل مرآة منصوبة تجتاز عليها الأشخاص فتتراءى فيها صورة بعد صورة أو مثل حوض تنصب إليه مياه مختلفة من أنهار مفتوحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.claim: Razi's summary traces the heart's continual effects to external senses and internal faculties, including imagination, appetite, anger, and temperament.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.anchor: مداخل هذه الآثار المتجددة في القلب ساعة فساعة إما من الظاهر كالحواس الخمس وإما من البواطن كالخيال والشهوة والغضب

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.claim: Sensory perception, appetite, and anger leave effects in the heart; when external perception stops, inner images persist and shift, changing the heart's state.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.anchor: إذا منع الإنسان عن الإدراكات الظاهرة فالخيالات الحاصلة في النفس تبقى وينتقل الخيال من شيء إلى شيء

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.claim: Razi's summary defines thoughts as fresh or remembered cognitions that arise in imagination after the heart had been heedless of them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.anchor: الخواطر ما يعرض فيه من الأفكار والأذكار وأعني بها إدراكات وعلوما إما على سبيل التجدد وإما على سبيل التذكر

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.claim: Thoughts move intentions, and intentions move the bodily limbs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.anchor: فالخواطر هي المحركات للإرادات والإرادات محركة للأعضاء

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.claim: Thoughts divide into those calling toward harmful outcomes and those calling toward beneficial ones; the good is inspiration and the blameworthy satanic whispering.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.anchor: فالخاطر المحمود يسمى إلهاما والمذموم يسمى وسواسا

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.claim: Because thoughts arise as events and an infinite regress is impossible, their causes must ultimately terminate in the Necessary Existent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.anchor: هذه الخواطر أحوال حادثة فلا بد لها من سبب والتسلسل محال فلا بد من انتهاء الكل إلى واجب الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.claim: Razi says al-Ghazali circles the intended issue, but the account requires further refinement before it succeeds.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.anchor: هذا الرجل دار حول المقصود إلا أنه لا يحصل الغرض إلا من بعد مزيد التنقيح

STUDYQURAN:13:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r1.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r1.claim: The verse offers two similitudes to illustrate truth and falsehood.
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r1.anchor: This verse provides two similitudes concerning truth and falsehood (Bg). In the first similitude, the water

STUDYQURAN:13:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r2.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r2.claim: In the water simile, the torrent churns up impurities that form useless froth and attach to trees and valley sides.
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r2.anchor: dirt and impurities, forming a swelling froth, which goes on to become attached to trees and the sides of valleys (Bg) and is basically useless.

STUDYQURAN:13:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r3.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r3.claim: Once the torrent subsides, its water becomes pure and useful to people in many ways.
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r3.anchor: When the torrent subsides, the water returns to its pure state (Bg) and is then useful to people in numerous ways.

STUDYQURAN:13:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r4.speaker: JJ, Kl
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r4.claim: The metal simile describes heating gold, silver, or copper ores to purify them and extract the desired metals; impurities rise as froth.
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r4.anchor: when retrieving precious metals such as gold, silver, or copper from the earth (JJ, Kl), the ores are heated over fire in order to purify them

STUDYQURAN:13:17/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r5.claim: Falsehood passes away like froth, while truth, like pure water and precious metals that benefit people, remains; 17:81 makes the same point.
STUDYQURAN:13:17/r5.anchor: Falsehood, like the scum generated by the torrent

TAB-FULL:v13p496/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r1.claim: The two parables compare truth and falsehood, and faith and disbelief: truth remains beneficial while falsehood vanishes.
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r1.anchor: وهذا مثل ضربه الله للحق والباطل، والإيمان به والكفر

TAB-FULL:v13p496/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r2.claim: The valleys carry water according to their capacities, the larger carrying more and the smaller less; the water represents truth and its rising foam falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r2.anchor: ذلك الماء الذي أنزله الله من السماء زبدا عاليا فوق السيل

TAB-FULL:v13p496/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r3.claim: A second parable is metal fired to obtain gold or silver ornaments and useful goods such as copper, lead, and iron; dross is falsehood and the useful pure metal remains.
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r3.anchor: ومثل آخر للحق والباطل، مثل فضة أو ذهب يوقد عليها الناس في النار طلب حلية يتخذونها أو متاع

TAB-FULL:v13p496/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r4.claim: The foam on floodwater and the dross of fired metals are carried off by wind or water, thrown against trees and valley sides, and become useless.
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r4.anchor: فيذهب بدفع الرياح وقذف الماء به وتعلقه بالأشجار وجوانب الوادي

TAB-FULL:v13p496/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r5.claim: The noun al-zabad is nominative under the construction “and among what they fire in the furnace is foam,” with the implied comparison to flood foam.
TAB-FULL:v13p496/r5.anchor: ورفع {الزبد} [الرعد: 17] بقوله: {ومما يوقدون عليه في النار}

TAB-FULL:v13p499/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas compares hearts receiving the parable to valleys receiving water according to their certainty or doubt: doubt does not benefit, while certainty does; foam is doubt and lasting water is certainty.
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها} [الرعد: 17]

TAB-FULL:v13p499/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the flood carries wood and manure, while useful water and purified metals illustrate good deeds, guidance, and truth that endure; on Judgment Day falsehood disappears and the people of truth benefit.
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله: {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا} [الرعد: 17]

TAB-FULL:v13p499/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r3.claim: Al-Hasan explains ornaments as gold and silver and useful goods as copper and iron; firing removes impurity, just as truth remains for its adherents to benefit from.
TAB-FULL:v13p499/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية} [الرعد: 17] إلى: {أو متاع زبد مثله} [الرعد: 17]

TAB-FULL:v13p500/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p500/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p500/r1.claim: Mujahid says each valley holds as much as it can; metal goods include iron, copper, and lead, whose dross resembles flood foam, and the water and foam represent truth and falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v13p500/r1.anchor: أنه سمع مجاهدا، يقول: " {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها} [الرعد: 17] قال: ما أطاقت ملأها

TAB-FULL:v13p500/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p500/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v13p500/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the foam's going as its freezing on the ground, and says the water that remains is the beneficial element; both images represent truth and falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v13p500/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قوله: " {فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء} [الرعد: 17] قال: جمودا في الأرض

TAB-FULL:v13p503/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r1.claim: Qatada says each valley carries water according to its size and the foam rises high; he describes three examples in one parable, with vanishing foam as falsehood and enduring water and refined metal as truth.
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها} [الرعد: 17] الصغير بصغره

TAB-FULL:v13p503/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r2.claim: Qatada explains al-jufāʾ as matter that clings to trees; the foam becomes useless and loses any hoped-for blessing, like falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها} [الرعد: 17]

TAB-FULL:v13p503/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r3.claim: Qatada identifies useful goods as iron and ṣufr (copper/brass); after its dross is removed, the useful metal remains, just as truth remains for its people.
TAB-FULL:v13p503/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها} [الرعد: 17]

TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r1.speaker: عوف
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r1.claim: A report reaching ʿAwf says valleys carry water by their size; foam is scattered by wind, while pure water remains for drink, crops, and use, and useful purified metal remains as well.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r1.anchor: قال: ثنا عوف، قال: بلغني في قوله: {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها} [الرعد: 17]

TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd applies the parable to truth and falsehood: foam and dross are useless, while water and sound jewelry remain and benefit people.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله} [الرعد: 17]

TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the small valley carries according to its small size and the large valley according to its large size.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {أودية بقدرها} [الرعد: 17] قال: «الصغير بصغره، والكبير بكبره»

TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says truth is like the floodwater that stays in the earth, while falsehood is like foam that does not benefit people.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r4.anchor: عن عطاء، «ضرب الله مثلا للحق والباطل فضرب مثل الحق كمثل السيل

TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r5.claim: Rābiyan means high or swollen, from rabā/yurbi; rābiya also names a raised mound, and 22:5 uses the same root for the earth swelling.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r5.anchor: من قولهم: ربا الشيء يربو ربوا فهو راب

TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r6.claim: The metals are called matāʿ because people make use of them; matāʿ broadly means anything people enjoy, as the poet's line about what remains before death illustrates.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#2/r6.anchor: وقيل للنحاس والرصاص والحديد في هذا الموضع: المتاع، لأنه يستمتع به، وكل ما يتمتع به الناس فهو متاع

TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r1.claim: Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlā says a pot “jafaʾa” when, as it boils, its foam pours out, or when it settles and no foam remains.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة معمر بن المثنى قال: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: يقال: قد أجفأت القدر، وذلك إذا غلت فانصب زبدها

TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r2.claim: Some Basran grammarians say the foam is absorbed by the earth; they connect jafā and ajfā to drying, while injafā describes a valley bringing down flood debris.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r2.anchor: زعم بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة أن معنى قوله: {فيذهب جفاء} [الرعد: 17] تنشفه الأرض

TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r3.speaker: العرب
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r3.claim: Arabic usage says jafaʾtu the pot means to pour out its foam, ajfaʾtuhu is another form, and jafaʾtu a man means to knock him down.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r3.anchor: وذكر عن العرب أنها تقول: جفأت القدر أجفؤها: إذا أخرجت جفاءها، وهو الزبد الذي يعلوها

TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r4.speaker: قيل
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r4.claim: One analysis treats jufāʾ as jufʾan, a verbal noun used as a noun; Arabic similarly uses forms such as qumāsh, duqāq, huṭām, and ghuthāʾ as nouns.
TAB-FULL:v13p503#3/r4.anchor: وقيل: {فيذهب جفاء} [الرعد: 17] بمعنى جفئا، لأنه مصدر من قول القائل

TABATABAI:13:17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17/r1.claim: After completing the argument against polytheists and distinguishing blindness from sight and darkness from light, the discussion contrasts faith and good works with shirk and evil deeds, their people, and their outcomes.
TABATABAI:13:17/r1.anchor: بيان لما أتم الحجة على المشركين في ذيل الآيات السابقة ثم أبان لهم الفرق الجلي بين الحق والباطل

TABATABAI:13:17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r2.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r2.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān defines a wādī as a low slope at the foot of a great mountain where rainwater gathers, and connects diyah etymologically with gathering substantial compensation for a slain person.
TABATABAI:13:17/r2.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان الوادي سفح الجبل العظيم المنخفض الذي يجتمع فيه ماء المطر، ومنه اشتقاق الدية

TABATABAI:13:17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r3.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r3.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān says qadr is a measure fixed in relation to something, whereas weight can increase or decrease; equal weight is qadr.
TABATABAI:13:17/r3.anchor: والقدر اقتران الشيء بغيره من غير زيادة ولا نقصان والوزن يزيد وينقص فإذا كان مساويا فهو القدر

TABATABAI:13:17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABATABAI:13:17/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads bi-qadrihā with a quiescent dāl; the vocalized and unvocalized forms are both dialectal, while the verbal noun is only lightened.
TABATABAI:13:17/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بقدرها بسكون الدال، وهما لغتان يقال أعطى قدر شبر وقدر شبر

TABATABAI:13:17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r5.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r5.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān explains iḥtimāl as forcefully carrying something on one's back; it can also mean enduring another's raised voice without anger.
TABATABAI:13:17/r5.anchor: قال والاحتمال رفع الشيء على الظهر بقوة الحامل له، ويقال علا صوته على فلان فاحتمله

TABATABAI:13:17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r6.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r6.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān defines zabad as the scum of boiling, such as the foam on a pot or flood.
TABATABAI:13:17/r6.anchor: والزبد وضر الغليان وهو خبث الغليان ومنه زبد القدر وزبد السيل

TABATABAI:13:17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r7.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r7.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān says jufāʾ is extended like ghuthāʾ and derives from hamzah; the valley casts it away as refuse.
TABATABAI:13:17/r7.anchor: والجفاء ممدود مثل الغثاء وأصله الهمز يقال جفأ الوادي جفاء

TABATABAI:13:17/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
TABATABAI:13:17/r8.claim: Abū Zayd uses jafaʾa for knocking a man down and ajfaʾa al-qidr bi-zabadihi for a pot casting away its foam.
TABATABAI:13:17/r8.anchor: قال أبو زيد يقال جفأت الرجل إذا صرعته وأجفأت القدر بزبدها إذا ألقيت زبدها عنها

TABATABAI:13:17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r9.speaker: الفراء
TABATABAI:13:17/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ observes that things gathered together often take the faʿāl pattern, as in ḥuṭām, qumāsh, ghuthāʾ, and jufāʾ.
TABATABAI:13:17/r9.anchor: قال الفراء كل شيء ينضم بعضه إلى بعض فإنه يجيء على فعال مثل الحطام القماش والغثاء والجفاء

TABATABAI:13:17/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r10.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r10.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān defines īqād as putting firewood into a fire and notes forms for fire being kindled or burning.
TABATABAI:13:17/r10.anchor: والإيقاد إلقاء الحطب في النار استوقدت النار، واتقدت وتوقدت

TABATABAI:13:17/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r11.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r11.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān defines matāʿ as something used for enjoyment.
TABATABAI:13:17/r11.anchor: والمتاع ما تمتعت به، والمكث السكون في المكان على مرور الزمان

TABATABAI:13:17/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r12.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:13:17/r12.claim: Majmaʿ al-bayān defines makth as remaining in a place over time, noting both fatḥah and ḍamma on the kāf and tamakkatha for tarrying.
TABATABAI:13:17/r12.anchor: والمكث السكون في المكان على مرور الزمان يقال مكث ومكث - بفتح الكاف وضمها - وتمكث

TABATABAI:13:17/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r13.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:13:17/r13.claim: Al-Rāghib defines falsehood as the opposite of truth: something that has no stability when examined.
TABATABAI:13:17/r13.anchor: وقال الراغب الباطل نقيض الحق وهو ما لا ثبات له عند الفحص عنه

TABATABAI:13:17/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r14.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:13:17/r14.claim: Al-Rāghib says truth and falsehood can describe statements and actions, citing claims about false gods, invalidated deeds, and mixing truth with falsehood.
TABATABAI:13:17/r14.anchor: وقد يقال ذلك في الاعتبار إلى المقال والفعال يقال بطل بطولا وبطلا وبطلانا

TABATABAI:13:17/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17/r15.claim: Falsehood is a supposed kind of existence that fails to match external reality on examination; truth is what does match. Belief is primary, and other things are described by analogy.
TABATABAI:13:17/r15.anchor: فبطلان الشيء هو أن يقدر للشيء نوع من الوجود ثم إذا طبق على الخارج لم يثبت على ما قدر

TABATABAI:13:17/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17/r16.claim: A statement is true when it matches reality, while an act is true when it attains its intended end or command; either is false when it fails its standard.
TABATABAI:13:17/r16.anchor: فالقول نحو السماء فوقنا والأرض تحتنا يكون حقا لمطابقة الواقع إياه إذا فحص عنه

TABATABAI:13:17/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17/r17.claim: An existent is true insofar as it exists; a nonexistent mistakenly believed to exist is false. A possible being is false insofar as wrongly assigned independence or permanence, though its existence itself is true.
TABATABAI:13:17/r17.anchor: والشيء الموجود في الخارج حق من جهة أنه موجود كما اعتقد كوجود الحق تعالى

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r1.claim: The verse is among the Qur'an's outstanding discussions of how truth and falsehood arise, appear, produce distinct effects, and follow God's unchanging practice.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r1.anchor: والآية الكريمة من غرر الآيات القرآنية تبحث عن طبيعة الحق والباطل فتصف بدء تكونهما

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r2.claim: Some commentators take the passage as two parables; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this and argues it is one parable that unfolds through several instances.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r2.anchor: وليس بمثلين كما قاله بعضهم ولا بثلاثة أمثال كما ذكره آخرون كما سنشير إليه إن شاء الله

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r3.claim: Other commentators count three parables; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that count and holds that the passage is one unfolding parable.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r3.anchor: كما ذكره آخرون كما سنشير إليه إن شاء الله وإنما هو مثل واحد ينحل إلى أمثال

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r4.claim: The poem illustrates that everything besides God is false in the relevant sense and that every pleasure inevitably passes away.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r4.anchor: ألا كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل وكل نعيم لا محالة زائل

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r5.claim: The subject of anzala is God, omitted because it is obvious; the indefinite māʾ denotes a kind, pure water unmixed with anything.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r5.anchor: وقوله { أنزل } فعل فاعله هو الله سبحانه لم يذكر لوضوحه، وتنكير { ماء } للدلالة على النوع

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r6.claim: The indefinite plural awdiyah signals valleys differing in size, length, breadth, and capacity.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r6.anchor: وتنكير { أودية } للدلالة على اختلافها في الكبر والصغر والطول والقصر وتغايرها في السعة والوعي

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r7.claim: Attributing flow to valleys is figurative, like saying that a waterspout ran.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r7.anchor: ونسبة السيلان إلى الأودية نسبة مجازية نظير قولنا جرى الميزاب

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r8.claim: The foam is called rābiyan because it floats and continually rises above the flood; floodwater makes the foam especially visible.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r8.anchor: وتوصيف الزبد بالرابي لكونه طافيا يعلو السيل دائما وهذا كله بدلالة السياق

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r9.claim: Rain falls on valleys of differing capacity, and each valley flows according to its own measure, with larger and smaller valleys taking their respective amounts.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r9.anchor: فسالت الأودية الواقعة في محل الأمطار المختلفة بالسعة والضيق والكبر والصغر بقدرها أي كل بقدره الخاص به

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r10.claim: Each flood carries conspicuous, elevated foam that covers the water from view.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r10.anchor: فاحتمل السيل الواقع في كل واحد من الأودية المختلفة زبدا طافيا عاليا هو الظاهر على الحس يستر الماء سترا

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r11.claim: The phrase's min marks the source material: metals and other earthly substances that can be melted and made into ornaments or useful goods.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r11.anchor: من نشوية ما يوقدون عليه أنواع الفلزات والمواد الأرضية القابلة للإذابة

TABATABAI:13:17#2/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r12.claim: People melt gold and silver for adornment, and iron and similar materials for tools and other necessities; their molten substance also produces foam.
TABATABAI:13:17#2/r12.anchor: طلبا للزينة كالذهب والفضة أو طلبا لمتاع كالحديد وغيره يتخذ منه الآلات والأدوات

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r1.claim: Here ḍaraba means that God establishes truth and falsehood, as the flood and its foam, and the molten material and its foam are established in the parable.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r1.anchor: فالمراد بالضرب - والله أعلم - نوع من التثبيت من قبيل قولنا ضربت الخيمة أي نصبتها

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r2.claim: The idiom of striking can imply establishing: the forceful act typically leaves something fixed, as a peg driven into earth by a hammer.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r2.anchor: فإن الضرب وهو إيقاع شيء على شيء بقوة وعنف لا ينفك عادة عن تثبيت أمر في ما وقع عليه الضرب

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r3.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r3.claim: Some commentators posit ellipsis or metaphor, supplying ‘the parable of truth and falsehood’; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds this an unsupported, unnecessary emendation.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r3.anchor: قول المفسرين إن في الجملة حذفا أو مجازا والتقدير كذلك يضرب الله مثل الحق والباطل

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r4.claim: An inserted ‘parable’ is unnecessary because the passage ends by saying God sets forth parables; the author's reading is complete without emendation.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r4.anchor: لكان موضعه المناسب له هو آخر الكلام وقد وقع فيه قوله تعالى { كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال }

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r5.claim: The two kinds of foam, separately mentioned earlier, are joined here because both share the property of being cast away; this supports one parable containing several instances.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r5.anchor: جمع بين الزبدين أعني زبد السيل وزبد ما يوقدون عليه وقد كانا متفرقين في الذكر

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r6.claim: Replacing the named water and metals with ‘what benefits people’ singles out the defining property of truth: human benefit, their sought end.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r6.anchor: وقد عدل عن ذكر الماء وغيره إلى قوله { وأما ما ينفع الناس } للدلالة على خاصة يختص بها الحق

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r7.claim: Foam from floods and smelting dissipates as falsehood, while pure water and useful earthly materials remain available for people's livelihood and enjoyment.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r7.anchor: فأما الزبد الذي كان يطفو على السيل ويعلوه أو يخرج مما يوقدون عليه في النار فيذهب جفاء

TABATABAI:13:17#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r8.claim: God's parables distinguish truth from falsehood and show people what benefits them in worldly life and their return to God.
TABATABAI:13:17#3/r8.anchor: الأمثال المضروبة للناس في كلامه تعالى يشابه المثل المضروب في هذه الآية في أنها تميز الحق من الباطل

TABATABAI:13:17-26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r1.claim: The demonstrative may point not to the preceding wording but to the external events themselves: visible natural occurrences are parables guiding discerning people to unseen truths, as worldly signs point to the unseen.
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r1.anchor: ولا يبعد أن تكون الإشارة بقوله { كذلك } إلى ما ذكره من أمر نزول المطر

TABATABAI:13:17-26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r2.claim: The divine outpouring is like rain: intrinsically free of forms and measures, it takes form from recipients, so each thing receives according to its capacity and readiness.
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r2.anchor: أحدها إن الوجود النازل من عنده تعالى على الموجودات الذي هو بمنزلة الرحمة السماوية

TABATABAI:13:17-26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r3.claim: Although recipient capacities determine how the gift is measured, those capacities remain within God's dominion and permission.
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r3.anchor: وإن كانت خارجة عن الإفاضة السماوية مقدرة لها لكنها غير خارجة عن ملك الله سبحانه وسلطانه ولا واقعة من غير إذنه

TABATABAI:13:17-26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r4.claim: The distribution of mercy among recipients necessarily brings up transient impurities, while the measured mercy remains stable; existence thus divides into enduring truth and vanishing falsehood.
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r4.anchor: وثانيها إن تفرق هذه الرحمة السماوية في أودية العالم وتقدرها بالاقدار المقارنة لها لا ينفك عن أخباث وفضولات تعلوها

TABATABAI:13:17-26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r5.claim: Truth is from God, whereas falsehood is not from Him, though it occurs by His permission; created things retain a lasting truthful aspect when false aspects perish.
TABATABAI:13:17-26/r5.anchor: والحق من الله سبحانه والباطل ليس إليه وإن كان بإذنه

TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r1.claim: To support the division between lasting truth and transient falsehood, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī cites verses saying truth is from God, creation was not made vain, God establishes truth, falsehood vanishes, and truth overwhelms it.
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r1.anchor: فهذه الموجودات يشتمل كل منها على جزء حق ثابت غير زائل سيعود إليه ببطلان ما هو الباطل

TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r2.claim: A truth does not oppose or displace another truth: it supports it toward completion and happiness. Apparent natural conflicts still cooperate toward God's ends, like an adze and wood serving a carpenter or balance pans serving a weigher.
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r2.anchor: إن من حكم الحق أنه لا يعارض حقا غيره ولا يزاحمه بل يمده وينفعه في طريقه إلى كماله

TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r3.claim: A defective adze or an underweight balance frustrates a sound purpose, corrupting without repair and harming without benefit; Qur'anic subjection verses express the underlying order.
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r3.anchor: وهذا بخلاف الباطل كوجود كلال في القدوم أو بخس في المثقال فإنه يعارض الغرض الحق

TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r4.claim: These principles apply to external realities and to knowledge and belief: true belief in a believer's heart is life-giving rain that remains a blessing, while false belief in an unbeliever is transient foam.
TABATABAI:13:17-26#2/r4.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الأصول كما تجري في الأمور العينية والحقائق الخارجية كذلك تجري في العلوم والاعتقادات

TABRISI:13:17-18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر
TABRISI:13:17-18/r1.claim: The Kufans except Abū Bakr read يوقدون with yāʾ, in the third person.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r1.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر يوقدون بالياء

TABRISI:13:17-18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:13:17-18/r2.claim: The remaining readers use tāʾ, addressing ‘you ignite.’
TABRISI:13:17-18/r2.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر يوقدون بالياء والباقون بالتاء

TABRISI:13:17-18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:13:17-18/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the tāʾ reading from the preceding address in ‘Have you then taken?’; it may also address all people generally.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي من قرأ بالتاء فلما قبله من الخطاب

TABRISI:13:17-18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:13:17-18/r4.claim: The yāʾ reading follows the earlier third-person mention of those who set up partners; it can also mean all people, as ‘what benefits people’ is general.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بالياء فلأن ذكر الغيبة قد تقدم في قوله أم جعلوا لله شركاء

TABRISI:13:17-18/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:13:17-18/r5.claim: Fī al-nār modifies yuqidūn: one can kindle upon something not itself inside a fire, as in the command to kindle clay.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r5.anchor: فجعل الظرف متعلقا بيوقدون لأنه قد يوقد على ما ليس في النار

TABRISI:13:17-18/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r6.claim: A wādī is the low ground at the base of a great mountain where rainwater gathers; diya is derived from the accumulation of substantial wealth paid for a slain person.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r6.anchor: الوادي سفح الجبل العظيم المنخفض الذي يجتمع فيه ماء المطر ومنه اشتقاق الدية

TABRISI:13:17-18/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r7.claim: Qadr is a proportionate relation without addition or reduction; wazn permits increase or decrease, and equality is qadr.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r7.anchor: والقدر اقتران الشيء بغيره من غير زيادة ولا نقصان والوزن يزيد وينقص

TABRISI:13:17-18/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:13:17-18/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads bi-qadrihā with sukūn on the dāl; both vocalizations are dialect forms.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بقدرها بسكون الدال وهما لغتان

TABRISI:13:17-18/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r9.claim: Qadr can be used in either vocalization, as in expressions for a span's measure; people also discuss destiny using both forms.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r9.anchor: يقال أعطى قدر شبر وقدر شبر والمصدر بالتخفيف لا غير

TABRISI:13:17-18/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r10.claim: The cited poem's use of al-qadar in its line about calamities witnesses the word's form.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r10.anchor:
قال:
ألا يا لقوم للنوائب والقدر

TABRISI:13:17-18/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r11.claim: Iḥtimāl means lifting something on one's back with the bearer's strength; iḥtamalahu also describes a loud voice that someone bears without anger.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r11.anchor: والاحتمال رفع الشيء على الظهر بقوة الحامل له ويقال علا صوته على فلان فاحتمله

TABRISI:13:17-18/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r12.claim: Zabad is the scum of boiling, including foam on a pot or flood.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r12.anchor: والزبد وضر الغليان وهو خبث الغليان ومنه زبد القدر وزبد السيل

TABRISI:13:17-18/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r13.claim: Jufāʾ is long like ghuthāʾ and originally has hamza; the verbs describe a valley producing foam and a pot shedding it.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r13.anchor: والجفاء ممدود مثل الغثاء وأصله الهمز يقال جفا الوادي جفاء

TABRISI:13:17-18/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r14.speaker: أبو زيد
TABRISI:13:17-18/r14.claim: Abū Zayd says jafaʾtu a man means I knocked him down, and ajfaʾtu the pot with its foam means I removed the foam.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r14.anchor: قال أبو زيد يقال جفأت الرجل إذا صرعته وأجفأت القدر بزبدها

TABRISI:13:17-18/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r15.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:13:17-18/r15.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says things that collect together commonly take the pattern fiʿāl, such as debris, cotton, ghuthāʾ, and jufāʾ.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r15.anchor: قال الفراء كل شيء ينضم بعضه إلى بعض فإنه يجيء على فعال مثل الحطام والقماش

TABRISI:13:17-18/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r16.claim: Īqād is putting firewood on a fire; related forms istawqada, ittaqada, and tawaqqada are also used for kindling or burning.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r16.anchor: والإيقاد إلقاء الحطب في النار واستوقدت النار واتقدت وتوقدت

TABRISI:13:17-18/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r17.claim: Matāʿ means something used for enjoyment or benefit.

TABRISI:13:17-18/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r18.claim: Makth is remaining somewhere as time passes; makatha, mukitha, and tamakkatha all mean to stay.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r18.anchor: والمكث الكون في المكان على مرور الزمان يقال مكث ومكث وتمكث أي تلبث

TABRISI:13:17-18/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r19.speaker: جامع العلوم البصير
TABRISI:13:17-18/r19.claim: The phrase fī al-nār is an implied circumstantial modifier of the pronoun in ʿalayhi; the sense is that the material is in the fire while being heated for adornment.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r19.anchor: قال جامع العلوم البصير قوله في النار متعلق بمحذوف في موضع الحال

TABRISI:13:17-18/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r20.speaker: جامع العلوم البصير
TABRISI:13:17-18/r20.claim: Ibtighāʾ ḥilya is a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial clause for the subject of yuqīdūn, meaning they seek adornment.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r20.anchor: ابتغاء حلية أي مبتغين حلية فهو مصدر في موضع الحال من الضمير

TABRISI:13:17-18/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r21.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:13:17-18/r21.claim: Abū ʿAlī's analysis is that fī al-nār is not governed directly by yuqīdūn; the gold is heated while it is in the fire.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r21.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون قوله في النار من صلة يوقدون لأن المعنى ليس على ذلك

TABRISI:13:17-18/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r22.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:13:17-18/r22.claim: Sībawayh treats zabad as the subject, mithl as its adjective, and مما توقدون as its predicate.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r22.anchor: وقوله زبد مبتدأ ومثله نعت له والظرف الذي هو قوله مما توقدون خبره على قول سيبويه

TABRISI:13:17-18/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r23.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:13:17-18/r23.claim: Al-Akhfash instead treats the phrase as raised by the adverbial expression.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r23.anchor: وهو مرتفع بالظرف على قول الأخفش

TABRISI:13:17-18/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18/r24.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18/r24.claim: Jufāʾ is accusative as a circumstantial expression, describing the state in which the foam goes away.
TABRISI:13:17-18/r24.anchor: وموضع جفاء نصب على الحال أي يذهب على هذه الحالة قال الشاعر

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r1.claim: God gives two illustrations of truth and falsehood: water with foam, and precious metals or other materials heated in fire with their slag.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r1.anchor: ثم ضرب سبحانه مثلين للحق والباطل

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r2.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r2.anchor: { أنزل من السماء ماء } أي مطرا

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والجبائي
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r3.claim: The streams carry water in proportion to their size: a small stream to its smallness and a large one to its largeness.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r3.anchor: والكبير على قدر كبره فسالت كل نهر بقدره عن الحسن وقتادة والجبائي

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the streams receive the amount of water apportioned to them.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r4.anchor: وقيل بقدرها بما قدر لها من مائها عن الزجاج

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r5.claim: The foam floats high above the water; pure useful water represents truth and Islam, while transient foam represents falsehood.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r5.anchor: أي طافيا عاليا فوق الماء شبه سبحانه الحق والإسلام بالماء الصافي النافع

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r6.claim: Another model makes Qur'an the descending water, with hearts taking their share of certainty and doubt according to capacity; water is certainty and foam is doubt.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r6.anchor: فالماء مثل اليقين والزبد مثل الشك عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r7.claim: The second example concerns gold, silver, lead, and other materials melted in fire.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r7.anchor: { ومما يوقدون عليه في النار } وهو الذهب والفضة والرصاص وغيره مما يذاب

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r8.claim: Adornment means ornaments made from gold and silver; useful goods include things made from minerals, such as vessels.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r8.anchor: أي طلب زينة يتخذ منه كالذهب والفضة { أو متاع }

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r9.claim: The heated materials also produce foam: their slag is impurity separated from the pure substance.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r9.anchor: ليتميز الخالص من الخبيث لها أيضا زبد وهو خبثها

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r10.claim: To strike a parable is to circulate it through lands until people use it as a familiar example.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r10.anchor: أي مثل الحق والباطل وضرب المثل تسييره في البلاد حتى يتمثل به في الناس

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r11.claim: The foam goes away as useless scattered matter.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r11.anchor: أي باطلا متفرقا بحيث لا ينتفع به

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r12.claim: What benefits people is pure water and useful substances; it remains in the earth and people benefit from it.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r12.anchor: وهو الماء الصافي والأعيان التي ينتفع بها

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r13.claim: The believer and his conviction resemble life-giving water and useful gold, silver, and other substances; the unbeliever and disbelief resemble foam, slag, and metallic dross.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r13.anchor: فمثل المؤمن واعتقاده كمثل هذا الماء المنتفع به في نبات الأرض وحياة كل شيء به

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r14.claim: God gives these examples to people concerning their religion.

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r15.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r15.claim: Qatāda counts three parables in one: Qur'an is rainwater and hearts are riverbeds, each taking an amount according to receptivity; reflection yields a great share and general assent a smaller one.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r15.anchor: قال قتادة: هذه ثلاثة أمثال ضربها الله تعالى في مثل واحد شبه نزول القرآن بالماء

TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r16.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r16.claim: Qatāda's second parable compares passing thoughts and Satan's whispers to foam above water: doubts arise from the soul, not from truth, and disappear while truth remains.
TABRISI:13:17-18#2/r16.anchor: فهذا مثل شبه الخطرات ووساوس الشيطان بالزبد يعلو على الماء

TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r1.claim: The third illustration makes disbelief useless dross and faith pure, beneficial water.
TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r1.anchor: فالكفر مثل هذا الخبث الذي لا ينتفع به والإيمان مثل الماء الصافي

TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r2.speaker: الحسن والبلخي
TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Balkhī take the parable phrase as the end of the preceding passage, then begin a new sentence with ‘For those who respond to their Lord.’
TABRISI:13:17-18#3/r2.anchor: وتم الكلام عند قوله يضرب الله الأمثال

THALABI:v5p282#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282#2/r13.claim: The rain and smelting images are two parables illustrating truth and falsehood.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r13.anchor: للحق والباطل مثلين. فقال عز من قائل

THALABI:v5p282#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282#2/r14.claim: Rain fills streams according to their capacity; the flood carries rising foam, while clear, useful water remains as the truth and disappearing debris is falsehood.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r14.anchor: أنزل هو من السماء يعني المطر ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها الكبير بقدره والصغير بقدره فاحتمل السيل الذي حدث على ذلك الماء زبدا رابيا

THALABI:v5p282#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282#2/r15.claim: Another view says the rain is the Qurʾān descending from heaven, with hearts receiving according to their measure of certainty or doubt, reason or ignorance; this too figures truth and falsehood.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r15.anchor: ويقال: إن هذا سيل القرآن ينزل من السماء فيحتمل منه القلوب حظها على قدر اليقين والشك والعقل والجهل

THALABI:v5p282#2/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282#2/r16.claim: The commentary begins a second image: material heated in fire for ornament or useful goods produces foam like the flood's foam.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r16.anchor: والمثل الآخر قوله: ومما يوقدون عليه في النار

THALABI:v5p283/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r1.speaker: حميد وأبو محجن وأبو وهب وحمزة والكسائي
THALABI:v5p283/r1.claim: Hamid, Abu Mihjan, Abu Wahb, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read يوقدون with yāʾ.
THALABI:v5p283/r1.anchor: قرأ حميد أبو محجن أبو وهب وحمزة والكسائي يوقدون بالياء

THALABI:v5p283/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v5p283/r2.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the yāʾ reading because the verse says the useful things benefit people and does not address anyone directly.
THALABI:v5p283/r2.anchor: واختاره أبو عبيد لقوله تعالى: ينفع الناس ولا مخاطبة هاهنا

THALABI:v5p283/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p283/r3.claim: Ḥilya means adornment made for wearing; matāʿ means something useful or anything one enjoys.
THALABI:v5p283/r3.anchor: ابتغاء حلية أي زينة يتخذونها أو متاع وهو ما ينتفع به

THALABI:v5p283/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r4.speaker: المشعث
THALABI:v5p283/r4.claim: Al-Mushaʿth's verse uses matāʿ for earthly valuables, identified as gold and silver.
THALABI:v5p283/r4.anchor:
قال المشعث:
تمتع يا مشعث أن شيئا

THALABI:v5p283/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p283/r5.claim: Iron, brass, copper, and lead are heated to extract useful goods such as jewelry and vessels.
THALABI:v5p283/r5.anchor: والحديد والصفر والنحاس والرصاص، ومنه يستخلص الأشياء مما ينتفع به

THALABI:v5p283/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p283/r6.claim: Like flood foam, smelting foam rises above pure useful metal; its impurity disappears, while useless foam resembles falsehood.
THALABI:v5p283/r6.anchor: زبد مثله يقول: له زبد إذا أنث مثل زبد السيل، والباقي الصافي من هذه الجواهر فيذهب خبثه

THALABI:v5p283/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v5p283/r7.claim: Abu ʿAmr explains jufāʾ through pot foam spilling away when it boils or settling until none remains.
THALABI:v5p283/r7.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: هو من قول العرب: أجفأت القدر النذر وجنات

THALABI:v5p283/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r8.speaker: القبتي
THALABI:v5p283/r8.claim: Al-Qubtī says jufāʾ is what a valley casts onto its banks; the verb can mean to knock someone down.
THALABI:v5p283/r8.anchor: وقال القبتي: الجفاء ما رمى به الوادي إلى جنانه

THALABI:v5p283/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
THALABI:v5p283/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī glosses jufāʾ as worn away and scattered.
THALABI:v5p283/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: جفاء يعني باليا متفرقا

THALABI:v5p283/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p283/r10.claim: Arab usage says the wind jafaʾa the clouds when it dispersed and carried them away.
THALABI:v5p283/r10.anchor: يقال: جفأت الريح بالغيم إذا فرقته وذهبت به

THALABI:v5p283/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r11.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v5p283/r11.claim: Some explain the word as separation from the earth; a valley is said to jafaʾa when it dries up.

THALABI:v5p283/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r12.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v5p283/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats jufāʾ as a verbal noun used like a concrete noun, as Arabs do with collective terms.
THALABI:v5p283/r12.anchor: قال الفراء: إنما أراد بقوله جفاء الجفاء لأنه مصدر، قولك جفأ الوادي غثاه جفاء

THALABI:v5p283/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p283/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p283/r13.claim: What benefits people remains in the earth, while the flood's foam quickly disperses; this is an example of truth and falsehood.
THALABI:v5p283/r13.anchor: وأما ما ينفع الناس من العوالق فيمكث في الأرض كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r1.speaker: عامة أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r1.claim: Most linguists define a wadi as an open space between mountains, hills, and rises where rainwater gathers and flows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r1.anchor: وهي جمع وادي، وهو كل مفرج بين جبال وآكام وتلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r2.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r2.claim: Shammar derives wadi from a verb meaning “to flow” and suggests that the word may name the flowing water itself, like a flood; the author prefers the first definition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r2.anchor: قال شمر (¬4): ودي: إذا سال، قال: ومنه الودي فيما أرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r3.claim: Abu Ali calls “the valleys flowed” an expansive expression meaning that the water of the valley or river flowed, with the noun “water” omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي (¬6): {فسالت أودية} اتساع، والمراد في: سال الوادي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r4.claim: Abu Ali notes that afʿila is an unusual plural for a faʿil noun and explains awdiya by analogy across faʿil/faʿil patterns and other broken plurals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي (¬6): {فسالت أودية} اتساع، والمراد في: سال الوادي، وجرى النهر، ماؤهما، فحذف المضاف، قال: والأودية جمع نادر في فاعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r5.speaker: غير أبي علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r5.claim: Another parallel is nād, “meeting place,” with the plural andiya, analogous to wadi and awdiya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p331/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: نظير واد وأودية، ناد وأندية للمجالس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r1.claim: Qadr means an amount or measure, including the amount of something as weighed; the author previously discussed its usage at 2:236.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r1.anchor: القدر والقدر، مبلغ الشيء يقال: كم قدر هذه الدراهم؟ وقدرها ومقدارها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r2.claim: Mujahid explains that each valley flowed as much as it could hold.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says a small valley receives its measure and a large valley its measure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج (¬4): الصغير بقدره، والكبير بقدره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari and al-Zajjaj gloss the phrase as the amount God determined to fill each valley, or the measure of its capacity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري والزجاج (¬5): (بقدرها) بما قدر (¬6) يملأها، قالا: ويجوز بمقدار ما يملأها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r5.claim: Qadr can be a verbal noun meaning what was apportioned for the valley’s filling, or a measure meaning its capacity; smaller valleys take less water and wider ones more.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r5.anchor: فإن صغر الوادي قل الماء، وإن اتسع الوادي كثر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r6.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r6.claim: Abu Ali takes the phrase to mean according to the valleys’ waters, since the intended meaning is not that the valleys flowed according to their own size.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r6.anchor: المعنى بقدر مياهها، ألا ترى أن المعنى ليس على أن الأودية سالت بقدر أنفسها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r7.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata’s transmission, interprets the water as the Qur’an and the valleys as people’s hearts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬3) {أنزل من السماء ماء} يريد قرآنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbari compares Qur’anic guidance to rain in its widespread benefit and believing hearts to valleys that hold water; al-Farra says hearts receive it according to their capacities and inclinations.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r8.anchor: شبه نزول القرآن الجامع للهدى والبيان بنزول المطر، إذ نفع نزول القرآن يعم كعموم نفع نزول المطر، وشبه الأودية بالقلوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r9.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r9.claim: The author of al-Naẓm likewise says the water represents faith and truth, and the valleys represent hearts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r9.anchor: الماء هاهنا إن شاء الله الإيمان والحق، فهؤلاء الذين سمينا جعلوا الماء مثلا للإيمان والقرآن، والأودية مثلا للقلوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the foam carried by the flood as doubt and unbelief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5): وهو الشك والكفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r11.speaker: الفراء والزجاج وغيرهما
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p332/r11.claim: Al-Farra gives zabad as foam; al-Zajjaj says rabi means floating high above the water, while others derive it from increase and swelling that makes the foam rise.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes mark “and from what you kindle” as the start of a second parable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين (¬3): ثم ضرب مثلا آخر فقال {ومما يوقدون عليه في النار}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r2.speaker: القراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r2.claim: The phrase is read with either second-person tāʾ or third-person yāʾ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r3.speaker: من قرأ بالتاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r3.claim: The tāʾ reading continues the preceding direct address, “Say: Have you then taken…,” or addresses people generally as those who kindle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r3.anchor: فمن قرأ (¬5) بالتاء فلما قبله من الخطاب، وهو قوله: {قل أفاتخذتم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r4.speaker: من قرأ بالياء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r4.claim: The yāʾ reading follows the preceding third-person reference to associaters; it may also refer generally to all people, as in the following phrase about what benefits people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بالياء فلأن ذكر الغيبة قد تقدم في قوله: [{أم جعلوا لله شركاء} ويجوز أن يراد به] (¬6) جميع (¬7) الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r5.speaker: جميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r5.claim: The material kindled over the fire is metal, including gold, silver, brass, iron, and copper.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r5.anchor: وأراد بما يوقد عليه في النار الفلز (¬9)، وهو ما يذاب من الجواهر كالذهب والفضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r6.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r6.claim: Abu Ali attaches “in the fire” to “you kindle,” since things can be heated over something outside a fire, as in Moses’ command to Haman at 28:38; here the metals themselves enter the fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p334/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي (¬2): وجعل الظرف الذي {في النار} متعلقا بتوقدون؛ لأنه قد يوقد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r1.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r1.claim: Gold and silver are heated to make jewelry; iron, brass, copper, and lead are heated to make utensils and other useful things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3) وغيره: الذي يوقد عليه لابتغاء الحلية الذهب والفضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r2.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r2.claim: Matāʿ means anything that people enjoy or use.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r3.claim: The foam produced by smelting is like the foam carried by the floodwater.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r3.anchor: زبد مثل زبد الماء الذي يحمله السيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r4.claim: God uses these natural processes as a parable for truth and falsehood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r4.anchor: كما ذكر من هذه الأشياء يضرب الله مثل الحق والباطل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r5.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the foam clause completes the first parable, while the truth-and-falsehood clause resumes and is completed by the final statement that God sets forth parables.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r5.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: هذا كلام فرق به بين الكلام الأول وبين تمامه؛ لأن قوله: {فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء} هو من الكلام الأول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r6.claim: The omitted phrase “for truth and falsehood” is understood from the earlier wording; Dhū al-Rumma’s poem similarly separates “lam” from its predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r6.anchor: والتأويل: كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال للحق والباطل، فاختصر الكلام اختصارا على ما سبق من ذكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r7.speaker: أبو زيد والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r7.claim: Jufāʾ is what the valley casts away; al-Farra defines it as throwing out or discarding, and says the word can name the gathered debris itself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r7.anchor: الجفاء (¬2) ما جفاه الوادي، أي: رمى به، قال أبو زيد (¬3): يقال: جفأت الوادي الرجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says jufāʾ is a circumstantial accusative and allows the verb “the valley cast out its debris” in either form, jafā or ajfā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬7) في باب الوفاق: جفا الوادي يجفا جفا أو أجفا، إذا رمى بغثائه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains that falsehood may temporarily rise above truth but God will erase it and give the eventual outcome to truth and its adherents; foam and metal slag are discarded, while useful water and pure metal remain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p335/r9.anchor: أن هذا مثل ضربه الله للحق والباطل، يقول: الباطل وإن ظهر على الحق في بعض الأحوال وعلاه، فإن الله سيمحقه ويبطله ويجعل العاقبة للحق وأهله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r1.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r1.anchor: يعني: المطر { فسالت أودية } جمع واد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r2.claim: Awdiyah is the plural of wādī, valley.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r2.anchor: جمع واد { بقدرها } بقدر ما يملأها. أراد بالماء القرآن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r3.claim: The measure is the amount that fills each valley; allegorically, rain is the Qur'an and valleys are hearts, which receive different shares: much, little, or none.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r3.anchor: بقدر ما يملأها. أراد بالماء القرآن، وبالأودية القلوب، والمعنى: أنزل قرآنا فقبلته القلوب بأقدارها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r4.claim: Foam is what rises above the water, high over it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r4.anchor: وهو ما يعلو الماء { رابيا } عاليا فوقه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r5.claim: Foam represents disbelief and falsehood: though it may appear to prevail temporarily, God erases it and gives the outcome to truth and its people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r5.anchor: والزبد مثل الكفر. يريد: إن الباطل - وإن ظهر على الحق في بعض الأحوال - فإن الله سيمحقه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r6.claim: The foam that goes away is what the valley casts out.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r7.claim: What remains is what benefits people, such as vegetation that grows for pasture.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r7.anchor: مما ينبت المرعى { فيمكث } يبقى { في الأرض }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r8.claim: The second parable concerns ores fired to make jewelry or vessels: gold and silver make jewelry, while copper and lead make utensils.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r8.anchor: يعني: جواهر الأرض من الذهب والفضة والنحاس وغيرها مما يدخل النار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r9.claim: The metals too have a foam-like dross, some of which the bellows expel.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r9.anchor: أي: مثل زبد الماء. يريد: إن من هذه الجواهر بعضها خبث ينفيه الكير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r10.claim: God sets out truth and falsehood through these examples; the verse has an advance and delay in its wording, with the meaning explained above.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:17-18/r10.anchor: وهذه الآية فيها تقديم وتأخير في اللفظ، والمعنى ما أخبرتك به

QASHANI:13:15-17/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r7.claim: Rain from the Holy Spirit's heaven is knowledge; the heart's valleys receive it according to their capacities, while the torrent bears away the soul's base qualities.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r7.anchor: من سماء روح القدس ماء العلم

QASHANI:13:15-17/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r8.claim: The fire is love, which kindles gnoses, unveilings, realities, and meanings; seeking adornment represents the soul's desire for perfections, while use represents moral virtues it enjoys.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r8.anchor: في نار العشق من المعارف والكشوف والحقائق والمعاني التي تهيج العشق

QASHANI:13:15-17/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r9.claim: The corresponding foam is the soul's conceit in seeing itself complete or adorned, its admiration and veiling, and other faults of its states.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r9.anchor: { زبد مثله } خبث كالنظر إليها ورؤيتها وتصور النفس كونها كاملة أو فاضلة

QASHANI:13:15-17/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r10.claim: Knowledge casts away the foam; what benefits people, true meanings and pure virtues, remains in the soul. The author links the cleansing image to 8:11.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r10.anchor: { فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء } مرميا به منفيا بالعلم كما قال تعالى:

QASHANI:13:15-17/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r11.claim: What benefits people is true meaning and pure virtue, which endures in the soul.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r11.anchor: { وأما ما ينفع الناس } من المعاني الحقية والفضائل الخالصة { فيمكث } في أرض النفس

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r10.claim: The valleys fill according to their capacity; empty matter flows with the life-giving grace of the water.
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r10.anchor: de vâdiler mikdarlarınca sel oldu boş maddeler feyz-i hayat ile aktı

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r11.claim: God also sent metals such as gold, silver, copper, and tin; people smelt and refine them for ornaments, tools, and commodities, producing foam like the flood’s.
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r11.anchor: İnsanlar bunları huliyyât veya kullanacak âlât[^6] ve edevât gibi emti‘adan bir metâ‘yapmak maksadıyla eritmek ve tasfiye etmek için üzerlerine ocaklar yakarlar

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r12.claim: The water and metal examples produce two similar foams, though the first involves no human craft and the second human effort.
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r12.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh birbirine benzer iki kef bulunur ki evvelkinde hiç insan sun‘u bulunmadığı hâlde ikincisinde insanların sa‘y u kasdı da bulunur.

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r13.claim: Foam represents falsehood: although it can surface while truth surges, it is ultimately cast aside and extinguished.
