ELMALILI:13:16-17/r13.anchor: Hak cereyan ve galeyan ederken her ne kadar bazen yüze çıkarsa da nihâyet köpük ve kef gibi atılır söner gider.

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r14.claim: Useful water remains in lakes and pools or enters the earth to feed wells, springs, and rivers; refined metals become goods that people use, as truth endures.
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r14.anchor: su kısmen göllerde, havuzlarda kalır, kısmen yerin damarlarına nüfuz eder; kuyular, pınarlar, ırmaklar olur. Süzülmüş madenler huliyyât veya emti‘a yapılır.

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r15.claim: Life-giving pure water from heaven represents the Qur’an and God’s revelation, which involves no human acquisition.
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r15.anchor: Semâdan inen ve medâr-ı hayat olan hâlis su Kur’ân’ın, vahy-i Hakk’ın temsîlidir. Ki bunda kesb-i beşerin hiç dahli yoktur.

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r16.claim: Smelted metals represent true knowledge inferred and synthesized through human effort.

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r17.claim: Both divine revelation and true knowledge acquired through human effort are, in essence, gifts from God.
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r17.anchor: Ve bunların ikisi de esas itibariyle dâd-ı Hak’tır.

ELMALILI:13:16-17/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r18.claim: God uses such parables to clarify many truths and call people to the truth.
ELMALILI:13:16-17/r18.anchor: Ve böyle birçok hakikatleri tavzih eden güzel temsillerle de hakka davet eyler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r1.claim: Water and valuable ore represent truth, while foam and dross represent falsehood: the useful and valuable endure, and the worthless passes away.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r1.anchor: Hak, suya ve cevhere, bâtıl ise köpüğe ve curufa benzetilmiştir. Su yerde kalır ve canlılara hayat verir, köpük ise sönüp gider

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r2.claim: The dross skimmed from heated metal is likewise discarded; even if falsehood seems to rise above truth for a time, truth ultimately remains.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:17/r2.anchor: Saflaştırılıp süs eşyası veya kap kacak yapmak için ateşte eritilen madenlerin üzerindeki curuf da atılır. Sonuçta değersiz olan yok olup gider, değerli olan kalır

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r1.claim: The majority of Bāqillānī’s Ashʿarite companions, including Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī, hold that at least a complete sura, or an equal amount, is inimitable.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r1.anchor: وهو قول الشيخ أبي الحسن الأشعري في كتبه

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r2.claim: On this view, even a passage the length of the short sura al-Kawthar is miraculous; no proof establishes failure to match anything smaller.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r2.anchor: قال فإذا كانت الآية بقدر حروف سورة وإن كانت سورة الكوثر فذلك معجز

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r3.claim: The Muʿtazila hold that every sura is independently miraculous.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r3.anchor: وذهبت المعتزلة إلى أن كل سورة برأسها فهي معجزة

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r4.claim: Some Muʿtazilites are reported to agree broadly with the Ashʿarites but require many verses, not a passage as long as a sura.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r4.anchor: وقد حكي عنهم نحو قولنا إلا أن منهم من لم يشترط كون الآية بقدر السورة بل شرط الآيات الكثيرة

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r5.claim: Because the challenge covered all suras without exception and the Arabs matched none, every sura is shown to be inimitable.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r5.anchor: وقد علمنا انه تحداهم تحديا إلى السور كلها ولم يخص ولم يأتوا لشيء منها بمثل فعلم أن جميع ذلك معجز

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r6.claim: The challenge to produce a discourse like it does not conflict with the Ashʿarite minimum: a complete discourse cannot fit into fewer words than a short sura.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r6.anchor: لان الحديث التام لا تتحصل حكايته في أقل من كلمات سورة قصيرة

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r7.claim: Alternatively, “a discourse like it” can be read as a challenge to the class or kind of discourse, rather than each individual instance.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r7.anchor: على أن يكون راجعا إلى القبيل دون التفصيل

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r8.claim: The challenge to humans and jinn refers to the Qurʾān collectively; the proof does not depend on their failing to reproduce the entire book from beginning to end.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r8.anchor: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r9.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r9.claim: Asked how one knows each short or long sura is miraculous, al-Ashʿarī answers that the Arabs’ inability to match each one establishes it.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r9.anchor: أجاب عن ذلك بأن كل سورة قد علم كونها معجزة بعجز العرب عنها

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r10.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r10.speaker: بعض الكبراء
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r10.claim: A senior authority suggests that the status of each passage as miraculous could instead be known through authoritative designation.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r10.anchor: وسمعت بعض الكبراء من أهل هذا الشأن يقول إن ذلك يصح أن يكون علم ذلك توقيفا

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r11.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r11.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r11.claim: Bāqillānī prefers the argument from Arab incapacity, while allowing that multiple routes to knowledge of inimitability may converge.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r11.anchor: والطريقة الأولى أسد وليس هذا الذي ذكرناه أخيرا بمناف له لأنه لا يمتنع أن يعلم إعجازه بطرق مختلفة

BAQILLANI:v1p254/r12.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r12.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r12.claim: The first method shows that the same basis for the Qurʾān’s inimitability exists in every sura, short or long, so the judgment applies uniformly.
BAQILLANI:v1p254/r12.anchor: فيجب أن يكون الحكم في الكل واحدا

BAQILLANI:v1p143/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p143/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p143/r1.claim: A letter sent to ʿAlī during the siege says the crisis has reached its limit and urges him to come to the sender’s aid, ending with a plea to rescue the sender before being torn apart.
BAQILLANI:v1p143/r1.anchor: أما بعد فقد بلغ السيل الزبى وجاوز الحزام الطبيين وطمع في من لا يدفع عن نفسه فإن أتاك كتابي هذا فأقبل إلي علي

BAQILLANI:v1p181/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r1.claim: The poem is good but not extraordinarily accomplished; it shows some affectation and artifice.
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r1.anchor: واعلم أن هذا صالح جميل وليس من الباب الذي يقال إنه متناه عجيب

BAQILLANI:v1p181/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r2.claim: “The fetter of wild beasts” is a fine but common conceit, easy to imitate; later poets deliberately compose such devices, whereas earlier masters produced them naturally.
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r2.anchor: فأما قوله قيد الأوابد فهو مليح ومثله في كلام الشعراء وأهل الفصاحة كثير والتعمل بمثله ممكن

BAQILLANI:v1p181/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r3.claim: “Twisting, charging, advancing, retreating” combines antithesis and simile, but poets describe a horse’s speed more delicately elsewhere.
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r3.anchor: وأما قوله في وصفه مكر مفر فقد جمع فيه طباقا وتشبيها وفي سرعة جرى الفرس للشعراء ما هو أحسن من هذا وألطف

BAQILLANI:v1p181/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r4.claim: The line’s four comparisons are artful but have been rivaled, and the device is readily achieved.
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r4.anchor: وكذلك في جمعه بين أربعة وجوه من التشبيه في بيت واحد صنعة ولكن قد عورض فيه وزوحم عليه

BAQILLANI:v1p181/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r5.claim: Poems fluctuate between excellence and weakness, ease and strain; by contrast, the Qurʾānic model maintains an ordered, clear, consistent composition through all its modes.
BAQILLANI:v1p181/r5.anchor: ولا سواء كلام ينحت من الصخر تارة ويذوب تارة ويتلون تلون الحرباء ويختلف اختلاف الأهواء

BURHAN:v1p492/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p492/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p492/r4.claim: God gives faith and the Qur'an two similes: water for the life they bring and fire for their illumination; the Qur'an is accordingly called spirit and light.
BURHAN:v1p492/r4.anchor: وقد ضرب الله تعالى لما أنزله من الإيمان والقرآن مثلين مثله بالماء ومثله بالنار

BURHAN:v1p492/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p492/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p492/r5.claim: As valleys flow according to their capacity, hearts receive the knowledge and faith God sends according to each heart's capacity.
BURHAN:v1p492/r5.anchor: فتسيل الأودية بقدرها كذلك ما ينزله من العلم والإيمان فتأخذه القلوب كل قلب بقدره

BURHAN:v1p492/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p492/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p492/r6.claim: The flood's high foam represents doubts and desires that accompany what hearts receive.
BURHAN:v1p492/r6.anchor: السيل يحتمل زبدا رابيا كذلك ما في القلوب يحتمل شبهات وشهوات

BURHAN:v1p492/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p492/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p492/r7.claim: Smelting gold, silver, lead, and copper also produces foam; as in the water simile, the foam disappears while what benefits people remains, like useful knowledge rooted in hearts through monotheism and worship of God alone.
BURHAN:v1p492/r7.anchor: كذلك العلم النافع يمكث في القلوب بالتوحيد وعبادة الله وحده

BURHAN:v3p148/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p148/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p148/r8.claim: The valleys flowed according to the amount of their waters.

BURHAN:v2p107/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p107/r1.claim: The Qur'an is the final scripture and is self-sufficient, while earlier books may require clarification by it; the Qur'an says it recounts most matters over which the Children of Israel differed.
BURHAN:v2p107/r1.anchor: ومنها جعله آخر الكتب غنيا عن غيره وجعل غيره من الكتب المتقدمة قد يحتاج إلى بيان يرجع فيه إليه

BURHAN:v2p107/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p107/r2.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr reports that most Ashʿarites, including Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī, hold that the smallest inimitable unit is a sūra, short or long, or an amount equal to one.
BURHAN:v2p107/r2.anchor: قال القاضى أبو بكر ذهب عامة أصحابنا

BURHAN:v2p107/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p107/r3.claim: On this view, even a single verse with as many letters as Sūrat al-Kawthar is inimitable; no proof establishes that opponents could match a smaller amount.
BURHAN:v2p107/r3.anchor: فإذا كانت الآية بقدر حروف سورة وإن كانت كسورة الكوثر فذلك معجز

BURHAN:v2p107/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
BURHAN:v2p107/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites hold that every complete sūra is inimitable; some require only a long verse and do not insist on the length of a full sūra.
BURHAN:v2p107/r4.anchor: وذهبت المعتزلة إلى أن كل سورة برأسها فهي معجزة وقد حكي عنهم نحو قولنا إلا أن منهم من لم يشترط كون الآية بقدر السورة

BURHAN:v2p107/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p107/r5.claim: Because the challenge called for all sūras and the challengers produced none, the whole range of those sūras is shown to be inimitable.
BURHAN:v2p107/r5.anchor: ولم يأتوا بشئ منها فعلم أن جميع ذلك معجز

BURHAN:v2p107/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p107/r6.claim: The challenge to produce a matching complete discourse does not conflict with the Ashʿarite minimum, since a complete discourse cannot be expressed in fewer words than a short sūra; it may also challenge a genre rather than every detail.
BURHAN:v2p107/r6.anchor: فلا يخالف هذا لأن الحديث التام لا تتحصل حكايته فى أقل من كلمات سورة قصيرة

BURHAN:v2p107/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p107/r7.claim: The challenge to all humans and jinn to produce the like of the Qur'an can address its kind or genre, since the proof is not that they cannot reproduce every part from beginning to end.
BURHAN:v2p107/r7.anchor: على القبيل لأنه لم يجعل الحجة عليهم عجزهم عن الإتيان بجميعه

BURHAN:v2p107/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
BURHAN:v2p107/r8.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī says each sūra is known to be inimitable because the Arabs failed to match it; another senior specialist suggested that knowledge could instead come by transmitted report.
BURHAN:v2p107/r8.anchor: قلنا إن أبا الحسن الأشعري قد أجاب عن ذلك بأن كل سورة قد علم كونها معجزة بعجز العرب عنها

BURHAN:v2p107/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p107/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p107/r9.claim: Al-Zarkashī prefers the argument from Arab inability: it shows that the same basis for judging the whole Qur'an miraculous occurs in every sūra, short or long, whereas the alternative requires estimating the inimitability by another method.
BURHAN:v2p107/r9.anchor: والطريقة الأولى أسد وتظهر فائتهما في أن الأولى تبين أن ما علم به كون جميع القرآن معجزا موجود في كل سورة قصرت أو طالت

BURHAN:v1p493/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p493/r1.speaker: قتادة
BURHAN:v1p493/r1.claim: Qatada says the verse combines three parables: as foam vanishes as useless scum, falsehood likewise disappears from its adherents.
BURHAN:v1p493/r1.anchor: روى ابن أبى حاتم عن قتادة قال هذه ثلاثة أمثال ضربها الله فى مثل واحد يقول كما اضمحل هذا الزبد فصار جفاء لا ينتفع به

BURHAN:v1p493/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p493/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p493/r2.claim: A sound prophetic report compares revealed guidance and knowledge to rain received differently by soils: some yield growth, some store water for people, and some barren ground retains or produces nothing; these represent people who benefit, preserve, or reject guidance.
BURHAN:v1p493/r2.anchor: وفى الحديث الصحيح إن مثل ما بعثنى الله به من الهدى والعلم كمثل غيث أصاب أرضا فكان منها طائفة قبلت الماء

BURHAN:v1p493/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p493/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p493/r7.claim: The author lists Qur'anic legal studies by school: al-Shafi'i first; al-Kiya al-Harrasi among Shafi'is; al-Razi among Hanafis; named Maliki scholars; and Qadi Abu Ya'la among Hanbalis.
BURHAN:v1p493/r7.anchor: وقد اعتنى بذلك الأئمة وأفردوه وأولهم الشافعي ثم تلاه من أصحابنا ألكيا الهراسي

SULAMI:v1p330#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r1.claim: God's pure pearl melted from shyness beneath His gaze of beauty; the flowing water signifies hearts purified and secrets made shy by that heavenly influx.
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : خلق الله تعالى درة صافية فلاحظها بعين الجمال فزابت منه حياء ،

SULAMI:v1p330#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r2.claim: As a flood sweeps filth from valleys, God's allotted light flowing into hearts removes heedlessness and darkness; water is the light apportioned eternally, and valleys are hearts.
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ^ ( أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية ) ^ هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى للعبد

SULAMI:v1p330#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r3.claim: Water represents kinds of divine gifts received according to each heart's share: guidance brings gnosis, love brings longing, and longing opens intimacy until hearts are immersed in witnessing.
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : ﴿ أنزل من السماء ماء ﴾ : أنواع الكرامات فأخذ كل قلب بحظه ، ونصيبه

SULAMI:v1p330#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r4.claim: Truthful spiritual states leave their blessings fixed in hearts; states lacking truth retain no good.
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ما كان من الأحوال صدقا . ثبت في القلوب بركاتها ، وما كان من غير ذلك فإنه لا يبقى فيه خير .

SULAMI:v1p330#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r5.claim: Water is the Quran as divine generosity; foam is pride in one's deeds before companions, which vanishes for people of tawhid, while the lasting benefit is certainty granted by God.
SULAMI:v1p330#3/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي : في قوله تعالى : ﴿ أنزل من السماء ماء ﴾ هو القرآن في صرف الكرم والفضل

ITQAN:v3p70/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p70/r1.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v3p70/r1.claim: Ibn Hajar says the report explains why the stoning verse’s recitation was abrogated: acting on the general wording’s apparent sense would be problematic.
ITQAN:v3p70/r1.anchor: قال ابن حجر في شرح المنهاج فيستفاد من هذا الحديث السبب في نسخ تلاوتها لكون العمل على غير الظاهر من عمومها

ITQAN:v3p70/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p70/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p70/r2.claim: The author suggests its recitation was removed to ease the community by not making its severe, burdensome ruling prominent in the codex; this also signals the desirability of concealment.
ITQAN:v3p70/r2.anchor: قلت وخطر لي في ذلك نكتة حسنة وهو أن سببه التخفيف على الأمة بعدم اشتهار تلاوتها وكتابتها في المصحف

ITQAN:v3p70/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p70/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ITQAN:v3p70/r3.claim: Al-Nasaʾi reports Marwan asking Zayd why the stoning verse was not written in the codex; Zayd points to the practice of stoning married offenders, and Umar asks the Prophet to let him write the verse, but is told he cannot.
ITQAN:v3p70/r3.anchor: وأخرج النسائي أن مروان بن الحكم قال لزيد بن ثابت ألا تكتبها في المصحف

ITQAN:v3p70/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p70/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p70/r4.claim: The author glosses Umar’s request to write the verse as asking permission or being enabled to write it.
ITQAN:v3p70/r4.anchor: قوله ( اكتب لي ) أي ائذن لي في كتابتها أو مكني من ذلك

ITQAN:v3p70/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p70/r5.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v3p70/r5.claim: Ibn al-Durays reports Umar affirming stoning as true; he considered entering the verse in the codex, but Ubayy recalls that Umar objected when he sought the Prophet’s recitation of it while people were behaving like donkeys in heat.
ITQAN:v3p70/r5.anchor: عن يعلى بن حكيم عن زيد بن أسلم أن عمر خطب الناس فقال لا تشكوا في الرجم فإنه حق

ITQAN:v3p70/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p70/r6.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v3p70/r6.claim: Ibn Hajar takes the exchange as indicating that disagreement was the reason the verse’s recitation was lifted.
ITQAN:v3p70/r6.anchor: قال ابن حجر وفيه إشارة إلى بيان السبب في رفع تلاوتها وهو الاختلاف

ITQAN:v4p344#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the flood and refining-metal parable represents hearts receiving guidance according to certainty and doubt: foam is doubt, while what benefits people and remains is certainty accepted by God.
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال هذا مثل ضربه الله احتملت منه القلوب على قدر يقينها وشكها

ITQAN:v4p344#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r5.claim: Ata says the parable is an example for the believer and disbeliever.
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج عن عطاء قال هذا مثل ضربه الله للمؤمن والكافر

ITQAN:v4p344#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r6.claim: Qatada identifies three analogies: foam that disappears is falsehood that perishes; water that remains and makes land fertile is truth enduring for its people; and fire refining gold or silver leaves the truth after removing impurity.
ITQAN:v4p344#2/r6.anchor: وأخرج عن قتادة قال هذه ثلاثة أمثال ضربها الله في مثل واحد يقول كما اضمحل هذا الزبد

ITQAN:v2p316/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p316/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p316/r4.claim: Biqadariha means according to its capacity.

ITQAN:v1p144/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ITQAN:v1p144/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda says Quran is so named because it gathers the suras together.
ITQAN:v1p144/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة وسمي بذلك لأنه جمع السور بعضها إلى بعض

ITQAN:v1p144/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r2.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v1p144/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says not every collection of anything or of speech is called Quran; the name reflects its gathering the fruits of earlier revealed books, or its gathering all kinds of knowledge.
ITQAN:v1p144/r2.anchor: وقال الراغب لا يقال لكل جمع قرآن ولا لجمع كل كلام قرآن

ITQAN:v1p144/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r3.speaker: قطرب
ITQAN:v1p144/r3.claim: Qutrub says Quran may be named for the reciter’s voicing and showing it from his mouth, comparing the Arabic expression for a camel that never miscarried.
ITQAN:v1p144/r3.anchor: وحكى قطرب قولا إنه إنما سمي قرآنا لأن القارئ يظهره ويبينه من فيه

ITQAN:v1p144/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r4.claim: The author prefers the position stated by al-Shafiʿi on the name Quran, without elaborating that position in this excerpt.
ITQAN:v1p144/r4.anchor: قلت والمختار عندي في هذه المسألة ما نص عليه الشافعي

ITQAN:v1p144/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r5.claim: Kalam derives from kalm, meaning effect, because it gives the listener an understanding not previously possessed.
ITQAN:v1p144/r5.anchor: وأما الكلام فمشتق من الكلم بمعنى التأثير لأنه يؤثر في ذهن السامع فائدة لم تكن عنده

ITQAN:v1p144/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r6.claim: The Quran is called light because it reveals subtle matters of lawful and unlawful rulings.
ITQAN:v1p144/r6.anchor: وأما النور فلأنه يدرك به غوامض الحلال والحرام

ITQAN:v1p144/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r7.claim: It is called guidance because it points to truth, using the source noun for the agent as an intensifying expression.
ITQAN:v1p144/r7.anchor: وأما الهدى فلأن فيه الدلالة على الحق وهو من باب إطلاق المصدر على الفاعل مبالغة

ITQAN:v1p144/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v1p144/r8.claim: Mujahid explains the title Furqan by saying the Quran distinguishes truth from falsehood.
ITQAN:v1p144/r8.anchor: وأما الفرقان فلأنه فرق بين الحق والباطل وجهه بذلك مجاهد

ITQAN:v1p144/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r9.claim: The Quran is a healing for inner illnesses such as disbelief, ignorance, and rancor, and also bodily illnesses.
ITQAN:v1p144/r9.anchor: وأما الشفاء فلأنه يشفي من الأمراض القلبية كالكفر والجهل والغل والبدنية أيضا

ITQAN:v1p144/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r10.claim: Dhikr refers to its exhortations and accounts of earlier peoples; it can also mean honor, as in the verse calling it a remembrance and honor for the Prophet and his people.
ITQAN:v1p144/r10.anchor: وأما الذكر فلما فيه من المواعظ وأخبار الأمم الماضية والذكر أيضا الشرف

ITQAN:v1p144/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r11.claim: The title Hikma is explained either by the Quran’s valid ordering of each thing in its place or by its containing wisdom.
ITQAN:v1p144/r11.anchor: وأما الحكمة فلأنه نزل على القانون المعتبر من وضع كل شيء في محله أو لأنه مشتمل على الحكمة

ITQAN:v1p144/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r12.claim: Hakim describes verses perfected in striking arrangement and meanings and protected against alteration, distortion, contradiction, and divergence.
ITQAN:v1p144/r12.anchor: وأما الحكيم فلأنه أحكمت آياته بعجيب النظم وبديع المعاني وأحكمت عن تطرق التبديل والتحريف

ITQAN:v1p144/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r13.claim: The Quran is called al-Muhaymin because it witnesses to all earlier scriptures and communities.
ITQAN:v1p144/r13.anchor: وأما المهيمن فلأنه شاهد على جميع الكتب والأمم السالفة

ITQAN:v1p144/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r14.claim: The Quran is called a rope because whoever holds to it reaches Paradise or guidance; habl also means a means or connection.
ITQAN:v1p144/r14.anchor: وأما الحبل فلأنه من تمسك به وصل إلى الجنة أو الهدى والحبل السبب

ITQAN:v1p144/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r15.claim: It is a straight, unbending path leading to Paradise.
ITQAN:v1p144/r15.anchor: وأما الصراط المستقيم فلأنه طريق إلى الجنة قويم لا عوج فيه

ITQAN:v1p144/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p144/r16.claim: Al-Mathani is explained as recounting nations after earlier scriptures, as repeating stories and admonitions, or as descending once in meaning and again in both meaning and wording.
ITQAN:v1p144/r16.anchor: وأما المثاني فلأن فيه بيان قصص الأمم الماضية فهو ثان لما تقدمه وقيل لتكرر القصص والمواعظ فيه

ITQAN:v1p144/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p144/r17.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v1p144/r17.claim: Al-Karmani transmits the explanation that the Quran descended once in meaning, then again in both wording and meaning.
ITQAN:v1p144/r17.anchor: وقيل لأنه نزل مرة بالمعنى ومرة باللفظ والمعنى كقوله ﴿ إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى ﴾ حكاه الكرماني في عجائبه

ITQAN:v1p160#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r1.claim: Zayd reports that the Qur'an was arranged from written fragments in the Prophet's presence.
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نؤلف القرآن من الرقاع

ITQAN:v1p160#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r2.speaker: البيهقي
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqi explains that this first gathering means arranging separately revealed verses into their sūras at the Prophet's direction.
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r2.anchor: قال البيهقي يشبه أن يكون أن المراد به تأليف ما نزل من الآيات المتفرقة في سورها

ITQAN:v1p160#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r3.claim: After the battle of Yamama, Umar urged Abu Bakr to gather the Qur'an because deaths among reciters might cause much of it to be lost; Abu Bakr initially objected that the Prophet had not done so, then agreed.
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r3.anchor: فقال أبو بكر إن عمر أتاني فقال إن القتل قد استحر بقراء القرآن

ITQAN:v1p160#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r4.claim: Abu Bakr chose Zayd for his youth, intelligence, trustworthiness, and prior work writing revelation; Zayd gathered the Qur'an from palm stalks, stones, and people’s memories.
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r4.anchor: قال زيد قال أبو بكر إنك شاب عاقل لا نتهمك

ITQAN:v1p160#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r5.claim: Zayd found the close of Sūrat al-Tawba with Abu Khuzayma alone; the sheets stayed with Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Hafsa.
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r5.anchor: ووجدت آخر سورة التوبة مع أبي خزيمة الأنصاري لم أجدها مع غيره

ITQAN:v1p160#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r6.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r6.claim: Ali called Abu Bakr the most rewarded person regarding the codices because he was the first to gather God's Book.
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r6.anchor: عن عبد خير قال سمعت عليا يقول أعظم الناس في المصاحف أجرا أبو بكر

ITQAN:v1p160#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r7.speaker: ابن سيرين
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r7.claim: Ibn Sirin transmits Ali's account that after the Prophet died, Ali vowed to leave home only for Friday prayer until he had gathered the Qur'an, and then did so.
ITQAN:v1p160#2/r7.anchor: من طريق ابن سيرين قال قال علي لما مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آليت

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r1.claim: Imaginative constructions cannot strictly be called true or false, and they vary through many forms and degrees.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r1.anchor: لا يمكن أن يقال إنه صدق وإن ما أثبته ثابت وما نفاه منفى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r2.claim: Abu Tammam's flood analogy makes poverty seem natural for a generous noble man, but its reasoning is only imaginative: water slides from heights for reasons unlike generosity and wealth.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r2.anchor: ومعلوم أنه قياس تخييل وإيهام لا تحصيل وإحكام

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r3.claim: The gray-hair conceit sounds true because one dislikes gray hair yet wants it to remain; actually the desired object is life, not gray hair itself.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r3.anchor: فأما كونه مرادا ومودودا فمتخيل فيه وليس بالحق والصدق بل المودود الحياة والبقاء

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r4.claim: Poets can praise or blame by attaching a judgment to an incidental shared feature that does not truly cause the virtue or defect, as with gray and youth.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p231#2/r4.anchor: فتعلقوا ببعض ما يشاركه في أوصاف ليست هي سبب الفضيلة والنقيصة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r1.speaker: قائل
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r1.claim: An imagined objector says treating existence as nonexistence, or vice versa, is not simile: it denies existence instead of transferring a shared quality.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r1.anchor: إن قال قائل أن تنزيل الوجود منزلة العدم أو العدم منزلة الوجود ليس من حديث التشبيه في شيء

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r2.claim: Jurjani grants the objection as framed but says one must preserve two distinct ways of assigning one meaning the name of another.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r2.anchor: فالجواب أن الأمر كما ذكرت ولكن تتبعت فيما وضعته ظاهر الحال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r3.claim: In the first route, calling ignorance death only cancels the person's claim to life, knowledge, discrimination, and sensation; it does not assert a resemblance.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما تنزيل الوجود منزلة العدم كما مضى من أن جعل الموت عبارة عن الجهل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r4.claim: Calling spent wealth still present because it leaves a beautiful memory denies that it has vanished absolutely; it is not a comparison with another thing.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r4.anchor: إنه باق لك موجود لم يكن ذلك تشبيها بل إنكارا لقول من نفي عنه الوجود

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r5.claim: The second route is a genuine likeness between meanings, as a question resembles death in how hateful and difficult it is for a free person.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p68#2/r5.anchor: أن السؤال يشبه في كراهته وصعوبته على نفس الحر الموت

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r1.claim: Jurjani divides metaphorical resemblance into three routes: sensible to intelligible, sensible to sensible through an intellectual likeness, and intelligible to intelligible.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r1.anchor: أنها على أصول أحدها إن يؤخذ الشبه من الأشياء المشاهدة والمدركة بالحواس

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r2.claim: Physical light suits proof and argument because visible light distinguishes objects, while proof illuminates the heart through the meanings conveyed by words, not their sounds.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r2.anchor: مدلول الألفاظ هو الذي ينور القلب لا الألفاظ

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r3.claim: Light is also borrowed for knowledge and faith; doubt and ignorance are darkness because they leave the heart like sight obstructed by night.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r3.anchor: النور يستعار للعلم نفسه أيضا والإيمان وكذلك حكم الظلمة إذا استعيرت للشبهة والجهل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r4.claim: Darkness can signify misguidance and disbelief because the person strays from the road, risks destruction, and may fall into a precipice.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r4.anchor: فلأن صاحبهما كمن يسعى في الظلمة فيذهب في غير الطريق وربما دفع إلى هلك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r5.claim: The balance or qistas is borrowed for justice because it conveys straightness and sound measure in an intelligible quality.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r5.anchor: استعارة القسطاس للعدل ونحو ذلك من المعاني المعقولة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r6.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r6.claim: Al-Jahiz calls kalam a measure for crafts and expressions, a qistas that reveals deficiency or excess, and a strainer that reveals clarity or muddiness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r6.anchor: استعارة الجاحظ في فصل يذكر فيه علم الكلام فقال وهو العيار على كل صناعة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r7.claim: Calling grammar the balance and measure of speech likewise transfers a bodily, visible instrument's quality to an intellectual discipline.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p50/r7.anchor: إذا قيل في النحو إنه ميزان الكلام ومعياره

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r1.claim: A strange simile joins remote things through a likeness that does not arise at first glance, but emerges after recollection, comparison, and extracting the intended feature.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r1.anchor: أن يكون الشبه المقصود من الشيء مما لا ينزع إليه الخاطر ولا يقع في الوهم عند بديهة النظر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r2.claim: More immediate associations include the sun's roundness and light with a polished mirror, embroidery with a rain-soaked garden, and a polished sword's gleam with lightning.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r2.anchor: كما ترى الشمس ويجرى في خاطرك استدارتها ونورها تقع في قلبك المرآة المجلوة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r3.claim: The line likening the sun to a mirror in a paralytic's hand is unusual because the resemblance is not quickly summoned by the mind.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r3.anchor: لا يسرع إلى تشبيه الشمس بالمرآة في كف الأشل كقوله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r4.claim: Kushajim likens lightning to a thief's finger, an unexpected image that illustrates a remote resemblance discovered by reflection.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r4.anchor: أرقت أم نمت لضوء بارق مؤتلق مثل فؤاد العاشق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r5.claim: Ibn Babak compares lightning's flash to a glowing spark and to a finger emerging from a curtain, extending the discussion of unfamiliar resemblances.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r5.anchor: ونضنض في حصنى سحائل بارق له جذوة من زبرج اللاذ لامعه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Mu'tazz compares lightning's alternation of spreading and contracting with a reader opening and closing a Quran, isolating its movement as the likeness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r6.anchor: وكأن البرق مصحف قار فانطباقا مرة وانفتاحا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r7.claim: The line comparing the lines of a book to thorn branches is another startling image whose point is found only by identifying a less obvious shared feature.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p135#2/r7.anchor: بلفظ يأخذ الحرف المحلى كأن سطوره أغصان شوك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r1.claim: This kind of metaphor leaves each word in its literal sense but makes the figurative move in the grammatical attribution: the day literally fasts, the night stands, and التجارة literally profits in فما ربحت تجارتهم.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r1.anchor: ولكن في أن أجريتهما خبرين على النهار والليل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r2.claim: The attribution in فنام ليلي وتجلى همي heightens the meaning compared with فنمت في ليلي; likewise فما ربحت تجارتهم has an advantage over فما ربحوا في تجارتهم.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r2.anchor: ليس حال المعنى وموقعه في قوله ، + الرجز + : ( فنام ليلي وتجلى همي ) كحاله وموقعه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r3.claim: In وسالت بأعناق المطي الأباطح, سالت retains its literal sense of flowing; the unusual figure lies in attributing the flow to the ravines.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p226/r3.anchor: كما أريد ب ' سالت ' في قوله ، + الطويل + : ( وسالت بأعناق المطي الأباطح ) غير السيل

AKHFASH:v2p404/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p404/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p404/r1.claim: Arabic has both qadr and qadar in expressions such as qadr/qadar shibr and qadartu aqdiru qadran; both vowelings also occur in the saying al-qadr.
AKHFASH:v2p404/r1.anchor: تقول: "أعطني قدر شبر" و"قدر شبر" وتقول: "قدرت" و"أنا أقدر"

AKHFASH:v2p404/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p404/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p404/r2.claim: The phrase is elliptical: from what they kindle for ornament or use comes foam like this foam.
AKHFASH:v2p404/r2.anchor: وقال {أو متاع زبد مثله} يقول: "ومن ذلك الذي يوقدون عليه زيد مثله"

DAMGHANI:v1p447/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r2.claim: Māʾ can stand for the Qur'an: as water gives people life, the Qur'an gives life to those who believe in it.
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r2.anchor: الثالث : الماء القران ز قوله تعالى فى سورة الرعد

DAMGHANI:v1p30/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r8.claim: Al-arḍ can mean the heart: what benefits people remains in the earth, that is, the heart.
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r8.anchor: الحادي عشر : الأرض يعني القلب قوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

DAMGHANI:v1p30/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r9.claim: Mujāhid interprets al-arḍ here as the courtyard of the congregational mosque.
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r9.anchor: الثاني عشر : الأرض ساحة المسجد الجامع - على قول مجاهد -

DAMGHANI:v1p438/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r7.claim: Yamkuthu means that what benefits people remains in the land; here it denotes benefit.
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r7.anchor: المكث النفع . قوله سبحانه فى سورة الرعد

DAMGHANI:v1p428/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p428/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p428/r1.claim: Matāʿ here denotes metal, such as iron, lead, and brass.
DAMGHANI:v1p428/r1.anchor: الرابع : المتاع المعدن من حديد ورصاص وشبه وصفر . كقوله تعالى فى سورة الرعد (( أو متاع زبد مثله )) يعنى هذه المعادن

DAMGHANI:v1p428/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p428/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p428/r4.claim: Mathal can mean a description; the source applies this sense to descriptions of the believers and of Paradise.
DAMGHANI:v1p428/r4.anchor: الثالث : المثل الصفة . قوله تعالى فى سورة الفتح (( ذلك مثلهم فى التوراة ومثلهم فى الإنجيل )) يعنى صفتهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r1.claim: Ṭughyān is exceeding a limit; anyone exceeding his limits in disobedience is a ṭāgh.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r1.anchor: الطغيان : مجاوزة الحد . فكل من جاوز حده في العصيان : طاغ

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r2.claim: The verb describes a flood bringing a great volume of water, a sea whose waves surge, or blood swelling and flowing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r2.anchor: وطغى السيل : إذا جاء بماء كثير وطغى البحر : هاجت أمواجه . وطغى الدم : تبيغ

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r3.speaker: الخليل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl recognizes ṭughyān and ṭughwān as variant forms, with both ṭaghaytu and ṭaghawtu as verbs.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r3.anchor: قال الخليل : الطغيان والطغوان لغة . والفعل : طغيت وطغوت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p171/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p171/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p171/r4.claim: The seventeenth sense of earth is the heart. Muqātil says the water in the parable is the Quran, so earth denotes hearts.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p171/r4.anchor: والسابع عشر : القلب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الرعد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r1.claim: Matāʿ is what a person obtains to fulfill a purpose or desire; istamtaʿa means obtaining something desired by the self.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r1.anchor: المتاع : اسم لما يحصل به الإنسان مقصودا أو مرادا ، تقول : استمتعت بالشيء إذا حصلت للنفس منه مقصودا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba gives matāʿ the sense of duration, as in the day extending, and also uses it for useful equipment and benefit, including a divorced woman’s mutʿa.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r3.speaker: شيخنا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r3.claim: The teacher defines pilgrimage tamattuʿ as performing ʿumra in the pilgrimage months, then enjoying clothing, perfume, and marital relations before ḥajj.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r3.anchor: قال شيخنا رضي الله عنه : ومتعة الحج أن يأتي بالعمرة في أشهر الحج قبل الحج ويفصل بينهما بزمان يستمتع فيه باللباس والطيب والنكاح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r4.speaker: شيخنا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r4.claim: The teacher defines the divorced woman’s mutʿa as what is given when no dower was fixed and the marriage was not consummated.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r4.anchor: ومتعة المرأة ما يدفعه إليها إذا طلقها ولم يكن فرض لها مهرا ولا دخل بها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r7.claim: A third sense is metal articles made for use or enjoyment, such as iron, lead, and copper.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r7.anchor: والثالث : ما يتخذ للاستمتاع من حديد ورصاص وصفر ونحو ذلك

FARRA:v2p60/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p60/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p60/r8.claim: The rainwater is a parable for the Qurʾan descending to people: hearts receive it according to their capacities and inclinations.
FARRA:v2p60/r8.anchor: ضربه مثلا للقرآن إذا نزل عليهم لقوله: (فسالت أودية بقدرها) يقول قبلته القلوب بأقدارها وأهوائها.

FARRA:v2p62/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p62/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p62/r1.claim: The useless foam represents what remains in the heart of an unbeliever who worships idols and is left with nothing; what benefits people and remains on earth represents the believer.
FARRA:v2p62/r1.anchor: وقوله: (فاحتمل السيل زبدا) يذهب لا منفعة له، كذلك ما سكن في قلب من لم يؤمن

FARRA:v2p62/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p62/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p62/r2.claim: When gold, silver, and copper are heated, the impurity extracted is foam like that on a torrent; jewelry and useful wares are what people seek from the metals.
FARRA:v2p62/r2.anchor: من الذهب والفضة والنحاس زبد كزبد السيل يعني خبثه الذي تحصله النار فتخرجه

FARRA:v2p62/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p62/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p62/r3.claim: The metals are heated to obtain ornaments or useful goods such as copper and iron; their scum is the corresponding foam.
FARRA:v2p62/r3.anchor: يقول: يوقدون عليه في النار يبتغون به الحلي والمتاع ما يكون من النحاس والحديد

FARRA:v2p62/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p62/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p62/r4.claim: جفاء is long in form and derives from جفأ الوادي غثاءه جفئا, when a valley sweeps away its scum; it is like غثاء and other collective mass nouns, can function as a noun, and denotes what disappears quickly.
FARRA:v2p62/r4.anchor: وقوله: (فيذهب جفاء) ممدود أصله الهمز يقول: جفأ الوادي غثاءه جفئا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r1.claim: The valleys flow according to their own capacities, whether small or large.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r1.anchor: {فسالت أودية بقدرها} أي: على قدرها في الصغر والكبر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r2.claim: Rābiyan describes foam rising high above the water.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r2.anchor: {فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا} أي: زبدا عاليا على الماء.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r4.claim: Matāʿ means utensils; smelted metals and minerals produce dross like water produces foam.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r4.anchor: {أو متاع} أو آنية. يعني: أن من فلز الأرض وجواهرها مثل الرصاص والحديد والصفر والذهب والفضة - خبثا يعلوها إذا أذيبت، مثل زبد الماء.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r5.claim: Jufāʾ is what a valley casts onto its banks; ajfaʾat a pot means it cast off its foam.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p227/r5.anchor: (والجفاء) ما رمى به الوادي إلى جنباته. يقال: أجفأت القدر بزبدها: إذا ألقت زبدها عنها (1) .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r1.claim: The water and metal similes teach that falsehood may temporarily rise over truth but God will erase it and give the final outcome to truth and its people.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r1.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله للحق والباطل. يقول: الباطل وإن ظهر على الحق في بعض الأحوال وعلاه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r2.claim: A generous rain fills each valley according to its capacity: the large receives much and the small receives little.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r2.anchor: ومثل ذلك مطر جود، أسال الأودية بقدرها: الكبير على قدره، والصغير على قدره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r3.claim: The foam that rises above floodwater represents how falsehood sometimes appears to prevail over truth; smelted metals likewise produce dross.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r3.anchor: فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا أي: عاليا على الماء كما يعلو الباطل تارة على الحق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r4.claim: The metals are gold and silver for jewelry and copper and iron for tools; their smelting produces foam like that on water.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r4.anchor: يعني الذهب والفضة للحلية، والشبه والحديد للآلة، حيث يعلوها مثل زبد الماء

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r5.claim: Water casts foam onto tree roots and valley sides, and a furnace casts off metal impurities; the useful water and pure metal remain, representing truth.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p196/r5.anchor: وكذلك خبث الفلز يقذفه الكير. فهذا مثل الباطل. وأما ما الماء الذي ينفع الناس وينبت المرعى فيمكث في الأرض

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r1.claim: متاع can mean a period of time, as in the statements that people have enjoyment on earth until a term and that it may be a trial and enjoyment for a term.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r1.anchor: المتاع: المدة، قال الله تعالى: ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r2.claim: In 13:17, متاع means useful implements or articles.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r2.anchor: والمتاع: الآلات التي ينتفع بها، قال الله تعالى: ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r3.claim: متاع also means benefit or usefulness, as in provisions for people and livestock, sea food for travelers, and empty houses that shelter visitors from heat and cold; it also underlies the divorced woman’s mutʿa.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p275#2/r3.anchor: والمتاع: المنفعة، قال الله تعالى: نحن جعلناها تذكرة ومتاعا للمقوين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p49/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p49/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p49/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas describes Paradise’s date palms as having emerald trunks, red-gold branches, leaves that become clothing, and fruit larger than jars and buckets, white as milk, sweeter than honey, softer than butter, and seedless.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p49/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نخل الجنة، جذوعها من زمرد أخضر، وكربها من ذهب أحمر

MAJAZ:v1p328/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p328/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p328/r1.claim: Rābiyan is the active participle of rabā yarbū, meaning swelling or rising.
MAJAZ:v1p328/r1.anchor: «فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا» (17) مجازه: فاعل من ربا يربو. أي ينتفخ

MAJAZ:v1p328/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p328/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p328/r2.claim: Matāʿ means what one enjoys or uses; al-Mushaʿath’s verse calls something that outlasts death matāʿ.
MAJAZ:v1p328/r2.anchor: «أو متاع زبد مثله» (17) ، وهو ما تمتعت به، قال [المشعث]

MAJAZ:v1p328/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p328/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p328/r3.claim: The phrase means God sets forth the truth and sets forth falsehood.
MAJAZ:v1p328/r3.anchor: «كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل» (17) أي يمثل الله الحق ويمثل الباطل

MAJAZ:v1p328/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p328/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
MAJAZ:v1p328/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr b. al-ʿAlāʾ says ajfaʾat al-qidr describes a pot whose scum spills out as it boils, or whose scum disappears when it settles.
MAJAZ:v1p328/r4.anchor: «فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء» (17) قال أبو عمرو [بن العلاء] : يقال: قد أجفأت القدر

MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r7.claim: Some read sūra with hamza and others without; the unhamzated form means a station or rank, as al-Nābigha's verse depicts honor above kings.
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r7.anchor: والسورة من القرآن يهمزها بعضهم، وبعضهم لا يهمزها، وإنما سميت سورة فى لغة من لا يهمزها

MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r8.claim: The Qur'anic plural is suwar with open wāw in both reading traditions, while a building's plural is sūr with wāw at rest; he cites al-ʿAjjāj for the latter.
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r8.anchor: وقالوا جميعا فى جمع سورة البناء سور الواو ساكنة، فخرج جمعها مخرج جمع بسرة والجميع بسر قال العجاج

MAJAZ:v1p17/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r3.claim: Abu ʿUbayda insists that the Qur'an was revealed in clear Arabic and rejects the claim that it contains non-Arabic words.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r3.anchor: نزل القرآن بلسان عربى مبين، فمن زعم أن فيه غير العربية فقد أعظم القول

MAJAZ:v1p17/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r4.claim: He rejects the claim that Ṭā Hā is Nabataean, identifying it instead as an opening expression and a name and emblem of the sura.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r4.anchor: ومن زعم أن «طه» (20) بالنبطية فقد أكبر، وإن لم يعلم ما هو، فهو افتتاح كلام وهو اسم للسورة وشعار لها.

MAJAZ:v1p17/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r5.claim: Similar-sounding words can share a meaning across Arabic and Persian without proving foreign origin; he compares Arabic istabraq/Persian istabra and Persian kūz/Arabic jawz.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r5.anchor: بالعربية والآخر بالفارسية أو غيرها. فمن ذلك الإستبرق بالعربية

MAJAZ:v1p17/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r6.claim: He rejects deriving sijjīl from Persian sang wa-gil and says the word means something hard or strong.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r6.anchor: ومن زعم أن «حجارة من سجيل» (105/ 4) بالفارسية فقد أعظم، من قال: إنه سنك وكل إنما السجيل الشديد.

MAJAZ:v1p17/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r8.claim: The Qur'an contains the rare vocabulary and meanings found in Arabic speech.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r8.anchor: ففى القرآن ما فى الكلام العربى من الغريب والمعاني

MAJAZ:v1p17/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r9.claim: Among Arabic rhetorical devices in the Qur'an are abbreviation, deletion, and withholding a predicate or report.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r9.anchor: ومن المحتمل من مجاز ما اختصر، ومجاز ما حذف، ومجاز ما كف عن خبره

MAJAZ:v1p17/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r10.claim: He lists constructions where singular wording refers to a plural and plural wording refers to a dual.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r10.anchor: ومجاز ما جاء لفظه لفظ الواحد ووقع على الجميع، ومجاز ما جاء لفظه لفظ الجميع ووقع معناه على الاثنين

MAJAZ:v1p17/r11.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r11.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r11.claim: Other number patterns include plural reports expressed as singular and a plural used as singular when paired with another singular.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r11.anchor: ومجاز ما جاء لفظه خبر الجميع على لفظ خبر الواحد، ومجاز ما جاء الجميع فى موضع الواحد إذا أشرك بينه وبين آخر مفرد

MAJAZ:v1p17/r12.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r12.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r12.claim: For two or more referents, a sentence may give the predicate to a singular or plural form and omit the report about the others.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r12.anchor: ومجاز ما خبر عن اثنين أو عن أكثر من ذلك، فجعل الخبر للواحد أو للجميع وكف عن خبر الآخر

MAJAZ:v1p17/r13.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r13.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r13.claim: He lists a construction that assigns the predicate of two or more referents to the first.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r13.anchor: فجعل الخبر للأول منهما، ومجاز ما خبر عن اثنين

MAJAZ:v1p17/r14.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r14.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r14.claim: He also lists a construction that assigns the predicate of two or more referents to the last.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r14.anchor: فجعل الخبر للآخر منهما، ومجاز ما جاء من لفظ خبر الحيوان

MAJAZ:v1p17/r15.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r15.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r15.claim: He includes forms that use human-style reporting for animals and inanimate things, and treats animals as the nonhuman beasts.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r15.anchor: ومجاز ما جاء من لفظ خبر الحيوان والموات على لفظ خبر الناس والحيوان كل ما أكل من غير الناس وهي الدواب كلها

MAJAZ:v1p17/r16.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r16.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r16.claim: Arabic may address an absent referent while meaning the present one.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r16.anchor: ومجاز ما جاءت مخاطبته مخاطبة الغائب ومعناه مخاطبة الشاهد

MAJAZ:v1p17/r17.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r17.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r17.claim: Arabic may address the present and then switch the address to an absent form.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r17.anchor: ومجاز ما جاءت مخاطبته مخاطبة الشاهد، ثم تركت وحولت مخاطبته هذه إلى مخاطبة الغائب

MAJAZ:v1p17/r18.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r18.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r18.claim: A letter may be added in the wording while the intended construction is understood by dropping it.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r18.anchor: ومجاز ما يزاد من حروف الزوائد ويقع مجاز الكلام على إلقائهن

MAJAZ:v1p17/r19.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r19.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r19.claim: An implicit element can be left unexpressed when context makes it unnecessary to state.

MAJAZ:v1p17/r20.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r20.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r20.claim: Repetition can serve emphasis, while concise phrasing can dispense with repeated wording.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r20.anchor: ومجاز المكرر للتوكيد، ومجاز المجمل استغناء عن كثرة التكرير

MAJAZ:v1p17/r21.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r21.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r21.claim: Arabic permits fronting and delaying elements, as well as assigning a predicate to something related to its original subject.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r21.anchor: ومجاز المقدم والمؤخر، ومجاز ما يحول من خبره إلى خبر غيره بعد أن يكون من سببه

MAJAZ:v1p17/r22.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r22.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r22.claim: Abu ʿUbayda concludes that all these figures occur in accepted Arabic speech.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r22.anchor: وكل هذا جائز قد تكلموا به

NAHHAS:v2p355/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p355/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v2p355/r4.claim: Commentators explain بقدرها as either filling the valleys to capacity or the amount measured out for each.
NAHHAS:v2p355/r4.anchor: قال أهل التفسير أي بقدر ملئها وقيل ما قدر لها

NAHHAS:v2p355/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p355/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p355/r5.claim: The flood clause is complete; Basran grammarians parse زبد as the subject in the next sentence.
NAHHAS:v2p355/r5.anchor: ( ومما توقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد ) رفع بالابتداء عند البصريين

NAHHAS:v2p355/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p355/r6.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p355/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i parses زبد as raised because the sense is “from what you heat over fire, there is scum”; it is useless froth like sea foam.
NAHHAS:v2p355/r6.anchor: وقال الكسائي ارتفع لأن معناه مما توقدون عليه في النار زبد قال وهو الغثاء وقد غثى يغثي

NAHHAS:v2p355/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p355/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p355/r8.claim: جفاء is circumstantial and comes from انجفأت القدر when a pot casts away its froth; it also means dross.
NAHHAS:v2p355/r8.anchor: ( فيذهب جفاءا ) على الحال من قولهم انجفأت القدر إذا رمت بزبدها وهو الغثاء أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa calls أودية an anomalous plural of واد, unattested elsewhere, explaining that فاعل can pattern with فعيل, whose plural takes أفعلة.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r1.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " شاذ، ولم نسمعه في غير هذا الحرف، ووجهه: أن فاعلا قد جاء بمعنى فعيل،

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r2.claim: The author counters that فاعل with the plural أفعلة is attested in جائز/أجوزة and ناحية/أنحية too.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r2.anchor: قلت: قد سمع فاعل وأفعلة في حرفين آخرين، أحدهما: قولهم: جائز وأجوزة، والثاني: ناحية وأنحية.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r3.claim: بقدرها may depend directly on سالت, or be an omitted modifier of أودية.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه متعلق بمحذوف لأنه صفة ل " أودية ".

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي والأشهب العقيلي وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r4.claim: The standard reading has an open dāl in بقدرها; Zayd ibn ʿAli, al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli, and Abu ʿAmr in one transmission use a quiescent dāl.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r4.anchor: وقرأ العامة بفتح الدال، وزيد بن علي والأشهب العقيلي وأبو عمرو في رواية بسكونها،

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r5.claim: احتمل here means حمل: the iftaʿala form has the meaning of the simple verb.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r5.anchor: و " احتمل " بمعنى حمل فافتعل بمعنى المجرد،

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r6.claim: Valleys is indefinite because rain falls in different places and not every valley runs; the flood is definite because فسالت has already introduced it, like repeating a previously mentioned noun.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r6.anchor: وإنما نكر الأودية وعرف السيل؛ لأن المطر ينزل في البقاع على المناوبة، فتسيل بعض أودية الأرض دون بعض

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r7.claim: The foam is scum from boiling; al-Nabigha's river line uses الزبد for the foam carried on the river's crests.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r7.anchor: والزبد: وضر الغليان وخبثه] قال النابغة:

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r8.claim: Other descriptions call it the torrent's carried froth and debris, bubbles cast onto its bank, or what a swollen valley throws up; these accounts are close in meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو ما يحتمله السيل من غثاء ونحوه، وما يرمي به [على] ضفته من الحباب.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r9.claim: The milk foam is called زبد; the word may derive from the preceding foam sense because of their shared color.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r9.anchor: قيل: مشتق من هذا لمشابهته إياه في اللون،

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r10.claim: زبدته زبدا means 'I gave him wealth'; it is used as a proverb for abundance.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r10.anchor: ويقال: زبدته زبدا، أي: أعطيته مالا، يضرب به المثل في الكثرة،

SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r11.speaker: الحديث
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r11.claim: A hadith promises forgiveness of sins even if they were like the foam of the sea.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17/r11.anchor: وفي الحديث: " غفرت له ذنوبه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر ".

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r1.claim: The prepositional phrase مما يوقدون is a fronted predicate and زبد its subject; مثله modifies it. The dross of metals such as copper, gold, and silver resembles water foam because both arise from impurities.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r1.anchor: هذا الجار [خبر مقدم، ومبتدؤه " زبد " ]. و " مثله " صفة المبتدأ، والتقدير:

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r2.speaker: الأخوان وحفص والباقون
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs read the verb with yāʾ, referring to people; the remaining readers use tāʾ in direct address.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وحفص " يوقدون " بالياء من تحت، أي: الناس، والباقون بالتاء من فوق على الخطاب.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r4.speaker: الفارسي والحوفي وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r4.claim: Al-Farisi, al-Hawfi, and Abu al-Baqa attach في النار to يوقدون.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r4.anchor: أحدهما: أنه متعلق ب يوقدون، وهو قول الفارسي والحوفي وأبي البقاء.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r5.speaker: مكي وغيره
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r5.claim: Makki and others attach في النار to an omitted participle, تقديره كائنا or ثابتا, reasoning that anything ignited upon something is already in the fire.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنه متعلق بمحذوف، أي: كائنا أو ثابتا، قاله مكي وغيره.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r6.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r6.claim: Abu ʿAli rejects the objection: one can kindle a fire over something outside it, as in 28:38, and a phrase can also reinforce meaning, as in 6:38.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي: " قد يوقد على الشيء وإن لم يكن في النار، كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r7.claim: ابتغاء is most plausibly a causal accusative; alternatively it is a verbal noun used circumstantially, meaning 'seeking' a jewel.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r7.anchor: فيه وجهان، أظهرهما: أنه مفعول من اجله. والثاني: أنه مصدر في موضع الحال، أي: مبتغين حلية،

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r8.claim: A حِلْية is something used for adornment; متاع is something used to meet needs, such as iron spades.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r8.anchor: فالحلية ما يتزين به، والمتاع: ما يقضون به حوائجهم كالمساحي من الحديد ونحوها.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r9.claim: The preposition من can mark origin, 'from it arises foam like water foam,' or partitive scope, 'some of it is foam.'
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r9.anchor: تحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن تكون لابتداء الغاية، أي: ومنه ينشأ زبد مثل زبد الماء. والثاني: أنها للتبعيض، بمعنى: وبعضه زبد.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r10.claim: جفاء is circumstantial; Ibn al-Anbari glosses it as dispersed, as in jafaʾat al-rih al-sahab, 'the wind cut up and dispersed the cloud.'
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r10.anchor: قوله: " جفاء " حال. والجفاء: قال ابن الأنباري: " المتفرق ". يقال: جفأت الريح السحاب، أي: قطعته وفرقته.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r11.claim: Alternatively, جفاء is what a torrent casts away; idioms describe foam being skimmed from a pot or a torrent's foam being cast off.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: الجفاء: ما يرمي به السيل. يقال: جفأت القدر بزبدها تجفأ، وجفأ السيل بزبده وأجفأ وأجفل،

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r12.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r12.claim: Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjaj reads أجفل with lām instead of the common form with hamza.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r13.speaker: أبو حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r13.claim: Abu Hatim objects to Ruʾba's reading with a disparaging remark that he ate mice; the author counters that al-Zamakhshari praised Ruʾba's eloquence.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r13.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: " لا يقرأ بقراءة رؤبة، لأنه كان يأكل الفار " يعني أنه أعرابي جاف.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r14.claim: The author explains Ruʾba's form from 'the wind scattered the flock into pieces,' giving it the same sense as the common hamza reading.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#2/r14.anchor: وقد وجهوا قراءته بأنها من أجفلت الريح الغنم، أي: فرقته قطعا فهي في المعنى كقراءة العامة بالهمزة.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r1.claim: The second account treats the hamza in جفاء as a replacement for wāw; the author says this seems to be Abu al-Baqa's choice.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r1.anchor: والثاني: بدل من واو، وكأنه مختار أبي البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r2.claim: The author prefers the hamza as an original radical because it remains throughout the root's forms; he questions waw because the root جفا does not suit the sense here and homonymy is not presumed.
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r2.anchor: وفي همزة " جفاء " وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها أصل لثبوتها في تصاريف هذه المادة كما رأيت.

SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r3.claim: The kāf in كذلك is accusative: 'in the likeness of that example, God sets forth [the truth and falsehood].'
SAMIN-DURR:13:17#3/r3.anchor: الكاف في محل نصب، أي: مثل ذلك الضرب يضرب.

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r2.claim: The command to declare God creator of everything is supported by the surah's earlier evidence for His oneness, then leads into a parable about believers and unbelievers.
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r2.anchor: أي قل ذلك وبينه بما أخبر الله به من الدلالة

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r3.claim: The valleys flowed according to the amount God had allotted them to hold; alternatively, the phrase means according to their capacity.
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r3.anchor: أي بما قدر لها من ملئها

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r4.claim: The foam is floating high above the water.

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r5.claim: The phrase means kindling material in pursuit of useful goods.

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r6.claim: Gold and silver are heated for jewelry; iron, brass, copper, and lead are heated to make useful articles.
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r6.anchor: والذي يوقد عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية: الذهب والفضة

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r7.claim: The metalwork produces foam like the foam on water.
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r7.anchor: و (زبد مثله) أي مثل زبد الماء

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r8.claim: Foam includes water froth and the dross of iron, brass, copper, and lead; it goes away uselessly, cast up by the valley.
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r8.anchor: أي: من زبد الماء، والزبد من خبث الحديد

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r9.claim: The beneficial water, silver, gold, iron, and other materials listed remain in the earth.
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r9.anchor: وأما ما ينفع الناس من الماء والفضة والذهب

ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r10.claim: The segment begins to compare the believer, his belief, and faith's benefit to the water in the parable.
ZAJJAJ:v3p144/r10.anchor: فمثل المؤمن واعتقاده ونفع الإيمان كمثل هذا الماء

ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r1.claim: Asad adds "once-dry" because awdiyah lacks the definite article al.
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r1.anchor: The interpolation of the adjective "once-dry" before "river-beds" (awdiyah) is necessitated by the absence of the definite article al before this noun

ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r2.claim: The indefinite form indicates that this rain fills only some riverbeds, leaving others dry.
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r2.anchor: According to Zamakhshari, this indicates that only some of the river-beds are streaming with water while others, not affected by this particular rainfall, remain dry

ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r3.claim: Wad normally means a usually dry watercourse or riverbed that carries water after heavy rain, and by extension can mean a river.
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n37/r3.anchor: term wad (or wadi in popular parlance) denotes, primarily, a "water-course" or "river-bed" which is normally dry

ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n38/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n38/r1.claim: Asad supplies the ellipsis that clear water remains beneath the scum.
ASAD-NOTES:13:17#n38/r1.anchor: while the water beneath remains clear

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r1.claim: She distinguishes general worldly provision or benefit, mata', from athath, which specifically means household furnishings; the cited contexts cannot be read as furniture.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r1.anchor: واضح أن المتاع فيها، عام لمتع الحياة الدنيا، وليس كذلك "الأثاث" بخصوص دلالته في آيتيه من الكتاب المحكم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r2.claim: A lexicon also uses mata' adjectivally for something exceptionally good and for a person complete in good qualities.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r2.anchor: وشيء ماتع: بالغ في الجودة، ورجل ماتع: كامل في خصال الخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r1.claim: Samarrāʾī calls these observations guiding signs of the Qur’an’s deliberate, uniquely controlled artistry, while the full inimitability exceeds any description.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r1.anchor: لا نقول: إن هذه هي مواطن الإعجاز، ولا بعض مواطن الإعجاز وإنما هي ملامح ودلائل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r2.claim: He presents the Qur’an as descending from the highest assembly through a noble angel, with inexhaustible signs of divine inimitability.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r2.anchor: إن هذا القادم من الملأ الأعلى، والذي نزل به سيدٌ من كبار سادات الملأ الأعلى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r3.claim: He imagines Qur’anic admonitions opening a spiritually closed heart and stirring awe and tears, invoking the call to humility and the Qur’an’s ease for remembrance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p9/r3.anchor: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمنوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ الله وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ الحق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p825/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p825/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p825/r1.claim: The singular السماء is broad in Quranic usage: it can mean clouds, rain, the open sky or space, or a roof/ceiling; the surrounding examples show these different senses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p825/r1.anchor: فالسماء كلمة واسعة جدا قد تكون بمعنى السحاب أو المطر أو الفضاء أو السقف

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Section III presents polytheism as uprooting the truth and justice on which the world rests, in conflict with the testimony of the universe’s laws.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: polytheism uproots the whole system of truth and justice on which this world stands

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The section alludes to truth’s victory over the evil opposed to it by the Qur’an’s revelation, with evil blown away like froth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: a very subtle allusion is given to the victory of the truth over evil in this conflict created between them due to the Qur’ ān’s revelation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Verse 17 advances the preceding argument in 13:16: polytheistic equivalence conflicts with the universe’s nature and God’s established practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Here, in this verse, one step ahead is taken and it is stated that these things are against the nature of this universe as well

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The water parable shows froth dissipating while useful water remains in the earth for its inhabitants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: froth is dissipated and water which is beneficial for the earth and its inhabitants remains in the earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: In the metal parable, impurities rise and evaporate when silver or another metal is melted, leaving the silver.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: after melting silver or any other metal in a pot, the filth comes to the surface and evaporates and the silver remains.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Together the parables show that the universe preserves what is beneficial and destroys what is not.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It wants to keep intact what is beneficial and destroy what is not.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God’s established practice pits truth against falsehood: falsehood’s froth evaporates while what benefits people remains.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He makes truth and falsehood strike one another. As a result of this collision, the froth of falsehood that appears is made to evaporate

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The rain in the parable represents the divine revelation now coming down.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the rain which is pouring down now in the form of divine revelation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The earlier flood-and-froth parable depicts froth disappearing, leaving the Qur’an and those who receive it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: very soon all this froth will vanish and whatever remains is the Qur’ān and its recipients.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The sentence suppresses an explanation: God gives parables so falsehood’s supporters see their fate and believers see their bright fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some words after “God in this manner relates parables” are suppressed. The overall sentence would be:

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r1.claim: After verbs such as ظننت and وددت, أن and its clause occupy a noun phrase slot, as though the speaker said ذاك.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r1.anchor: فظننت عاملة كأنك قلت ظننت ذاك وكذلك وددت أنه ذاهب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r2.claim: After لو or لولا, أن clauses function like ذا; Sibawayh illustrates the construction with a Quranic example and a line of poetry.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r2.anchor: فأن مبنية على لو كما كانت مبنية على لولا كأنك قلت لو ذاك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r3.claim: In ما رأيته مذ أن الله خلقني, أن occupies a noun slot equivalent to ذاك after مذ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r3.anchor: مذ أن الله خلقني فقال أن في موضع اسم كأنه قال مذ

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r4.author: Sībawayh
