IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r1.claim: The complete image has rain flowing over hills into valleys of varying capacities, carrying foam that soon vanishes while water stays in the earth for people’s use.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r1.anchor: شبه ذلك كله بهيئة نزول الماء فانحداره على الجبال والتلال وسيلانه في الأودية على اختلاف مقاديرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r2.claim: The fāʾs mark the consequences of the rain in sequence; because the intended comparison is the whole scene, this also supports breaking it into component comparisons and makes the parable especially eloquent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r2.anchor: ولما كان المقصود التشبيه بالهيئة كلها جيء في حكاية ما ترتب على إنزال الماء بالعطف بفاء التفريع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r3.claim: A Prophetic report compares the guidance and knowledge brought by the Messenger to abundant rain: fertile land grows plants, rugged land stores water for people, and barren land benefits from neither; it likens these to learners who teach and those who reject guidance. No grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r3.anchor: مثل ما بعثني الله به من الهدى والعلم كمثل الغيث الكثير أصاب أرضا فكان منها نقية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r4.claim: An awdiya is the plural of wādī, a broad, extended hollow through which a flood runs; he points back to 9:121.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r4.anchor: والأودية : جمع الوادي ، وهو الحفير المتسع الممتد من الأرض الذي يجري فيه السيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r5.claim: Qadr means measurement or proportion, and بِقَدَرِهَا is circumstantial from أودية.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r5.anchor: والقدر بفتحتين : التقدير ، فقوله : بقدرها } في موضع الحال من { أودية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r6.claim: Valley beds usually fit the volume of water they carry without overflowing, making this a scene of useful water without damage, unlike destructive floods that sweep crops, homes, and livestock.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r6.anchor: وذكره لأنه من مواضع العبرة ، وهو أن كانت أخاديد الأودية على قدر ما تحتمله من السيول بحيث لا تفيض عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r7.claim: Differences in valley size and water capacity also represent differences in people’s receptivity to what God sends; the comparison is complete here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p117/r7.anchor: وأيضا هو دال على تفاوت الأودية في مقادير المياه . ولذلك حظ من التشبيه وهو اختلاف الناس في قابلية الانتفاع بما نزل من عند الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r1.claim: The sentence about what is kindled in fire is parenthetical, inserted between the flood’s foam and the concluding statement about foam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r1.anchor: وجملة { ومما توقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زيد مثله } معترضة بين جملة { فاحتمل } الخ وجملة { فأما الزبد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r2.claim: A second, familiar image makes the parable clear to Meccans who may not see valley floods: Mecca had goldsmiths, as the report about idhkhir indicates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r2.anchor: وهذا تمثيل آخر ورد استطرادا عقب ذكر نظيره يفيد تقريب التمثيل لقوم لم يشاهدوا سيول الأودية من سكان القرى مثل أهل مكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r3.claim: Smelting gold or silver in crucibles throws off useless dross, while the metal remains fit for ornaments or currency; this mirrors one group’s failure to benefit from what another uses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r3.anchor: فإنه يقذف زبدا ينتفي عنه وهو الخبث وهو غير صالح لشيء في حين صلاح معدنه لاتخاذه حلية أو متاعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r4.claim: He cites a hadith likening the removal of dross to bellows removing impurities from iron; no chain or grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث ( كما ينفي الكير خبث الحديد )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r5.claim: This is a second near simile, like the paired fire and rain comparisons in 2:19; the phrase زبد مثله signals the matching foam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r5.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا ثم قوله : أو كصيب من السماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r6.claim: Labīd’s lines about smoke rising from a fire offer a close poetic parallel to this image.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r6.anchor: وأقرب إلى ما هنا قول لبيد : فتنازعا سبطا يطير ظلاله كدخان مشعلة يشب ضرامها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r7.claim: Putting زبد before its subject foregrounds this notable feature and creates suspense; foam floats on both water, the thinnest material, and metal, the densest, as a natural law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r7.anchor: وتقديم المسند على المسند إليه في هذه الجملة للاهتمام بالمسند لأنه موضع اعتبار أيضا ببديع صنع الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r8.claim: A Prophetic description of Hell similarly builds anticipation by first mentioning hooks like saʿdān thorns and then asking whether the listeners have seen those thorns; no grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r8.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في وصف جهنم ( فإذا فيها كلاليب مثل حسك السعدان هل رأيتم حسك السعدان )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r9.claim: The relative phrase replaces explicit names for gold and silver because it is concise and lets the relevant process remain in focus; naming the metals and then describing the necessary source of foam would be longer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p118/r9.anchor: وعدل عن تسمية الذهب والفضة إلى الموصولية بقوله تعالى : { ومما توقدون عليه في النار } لأنها أخصر وأجمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r1.claim: Omitting the names gold and silver signals detachment from people’s fascination with them, since custom treats their names with reverence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r1.anchor: ولأن في العدول عن ذكر اسم الذهب والفضة إعراضا يؤذن بقلة الاكتراث بهما ترفعا عن ولع الناس بهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r2.claim: The preposition من in مما is partitive in origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r2.anchor: و { من } في قوله : { ومما توقدون } ابتدائية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r3.claim: ابتغاء حلية أو متاع is a purpose-object attached to kindling; it clarifies the relative phrase and embeds the favor of making these desired resources available to people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r3.anchor: و { ابتغاء حلية أو متاع } مفعول لأجله متعلق ب { توقدون } . ذكر لإيضاح المراد من الصلة ولإدماج ما فيه من منة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r4.claim: Ḥilya is an ornament worn for adornment, meaning a crafted piece of jewelry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r4.anchor: والحلية : ما يتحلى به ، أي يتزين وهو المصوغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r5.claim: Matāʿ is what people use and benefit from here: coined gold and silver used in exchange.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r5.anchor: والمتاع : ما يتمتع به وينتفع ، وذلك المسكوك الذي يتعامل به الناس من الذهب والفضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r6.claim: Most reciters read توقدون with second-person tāʾ; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and Khalaf read it with third-person yāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { توقدون } بفوقية في أوله على الخطاب ، وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف بتحتية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r7.claim: This parenthetical sentence sums up the parable; يضرب means to explain and set forth an example, as at 2:26.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r7.anchor: وجملة { كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل } معترضة ، هي فذلكة التمثيل ببيان الغرض منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r8.claim: A noun is omitted after يضرب: the intended wording is “God sets forth the example of truth and falsehood,” implied by the verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r8.anchor: فحذف مضاف في قوله : يضرب الله الحق } ، والتقدير : يضرب الله مثل الحق والباطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r9.claim: The preposition before الحق is omitted, treating the genitive complement as if it were the omitted noun itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r9.anchor: وحذف الجار من { الحق } لتنزيل المضاف إليه منزلة المضاف المحذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r10.claim: Foam represents falsehood and water represents truth; their disappearance and persistence become a promise and warning that the people of truth endure while falsehood vanishes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p119/r10.anchor: وقد علم أن الزبد مثل للباطل وأن الماء مثل للحق ، فارتقى عند ذلك إلى ما في المثلين من صفتي البقاء والزوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r1.claim: The foam clause branches from the flood's carrying foam; opening with أما emphasizes the conclusion and directs attention to the parable's subtle glad tidings and warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r1.anchor: فجملة فأما الزبد } معطوفة على جملة { فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r2.claim: جفاء means cast-off matter that is thrown away.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r3.claim: The foam's disappearance warns that the polytheists will perish in killing while the believers remain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r3.anchor: وهذا وعيد للمشركين بأنهم سيبيدون بالقتل ويبقى المؤمنون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r4.claim: Calling the water what benefits people hints why it remains and indirectly invites polytheists to see that they do not benefit people, paralleling the righteous inheriting earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r4.anchor: وعبر عن الماء بما ينفع الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r5.claim: The matching comparison between useful water and gold or silver, and between foam and their dross, is left unstated because it is readily understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r5.anchor: واكتفي بذكر وجه شبه النافع بالماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r6.claim: The closing sentence is a generalizing coda broader than the preceding particular parable, while also reaffirming it because the general includes the particular.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r6.anchor: مستأنفة تذييلية لما في لفظ { الأمثال } من العموم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p120/r7.claim: The demonstrative points back to the water parable, honoring its wisdom, admonitions, allusive force, Qur'anic eloquence, and challenge to polytheists; the parable ends here.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r1.claim: Qur’an names the revealed speech collected in the 114 suras from al-Fatiha to al-Nas; it became a proper name for this revelation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r2.claim: The name may be a verbal noun on the faʿlan pattern or a proper name; Ibn Ashur derives it from reading because the first revelation began with “Read in your Lord’s name.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r2.anchor: لأنه مشتق من القراءة لأن أول ما بدئ به الرسول من الوحي ) اقرأ باسم ربك (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce Qur’an with hamza throughout the revelation; Ibn Kathir alone reads it with a lengthened alif after the ra, following a Hijazi dialect that lightens hamza.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r3.anchor: ولذلك اتفق أكثر القراء على قراءة لفظ قرآن مهموزا حيثما وقع في التنزيل ولم يخالفهم إلا ابن كثير قرأه بفتح الراء بعدها ألف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur says variant readings generally agree in the meaning of the word despite differing in its form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r4.anchor: والأصل توافق القراءات في مدلول اللفظ المختلف في قراءته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r5.claim: A reported alternative derives Qur’an from qarn, joining, because its suras, verses, and letters are joined; on that view it is not from qara’a, and Ibn Kathir’s form fits as another name for the Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r5.anchor: وقيل هو قرآن بوزن فعال ، من القرن بين الأشياء أي الجمع بينها لأنه قرنت سوره بعضها ببعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r6.claim: Some derive Qur’an from qarina, signifying mutually confirming verses, but Ibn Ashur rejects the proposed collective plural because this form’s known plurals do not include it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r6.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن قرآن جمع قرينه أي اسم جمع ، إذ لا يجمع مثل قرينه على وزن فعال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r7.claim: Qur’an is the most famous and frequently used name for Muhammad’s revelation; al-Itqan lists more than twenty names or descriptions, with six commonly used names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r7.anchor: وهو أشهر أسمائه وأكثرها ورودا في آياته وأشهرها دورانا على ألسنة السلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r8.claim: The other six common names are al-Tanzil, al-Kitab, al-Furqan, al-Dhikr, al-Wahy, and Kalam Allah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r8.anchor: والذي اشتهر إطلاقه عليه منها ستة : التنزيل ، والكتاب ، والفرقان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r9.claim: Al-Furqan originally means what distinguishes truth from falsehood; it is a verbal noun used for the Battle of Badr’s day and became a proper name for the Qur’an, like Torah and Gospel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r9.anchor: فأما الفرقان فهو في الأصل اسم لما يفرق به بين الحق والباطل وهو مصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r10.claim: Al Imran first calls the revelation the Book, then calls it al-Furqan after naming Torah and Gospel, signaling that al-Furqan is the proper name of Muhammad’s Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r10.anchor: فوصفه أولا بالكتاب وهو اسم الجنس العام ثم عبر عنه باسم الفرقان عقب ذكر التوراة والإنجيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r11.claim: The Qur’an merits the name al-Furqan because it distinguishes truth from falsehood through proofs and parables, especially in its teaching of monotheism and God’s attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r11.anchor: ووجه تسميته الفرقان أنه امتاز عن بقية الكتب السماوية بكثرة ما فيه من بيان التفرقة بين الحق والباطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r12.claim: The Qur’an condenses the virtues attributed to Muhammad’s companions in earlier scriptures into the declaration that the community is the best nation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r12.anchor: فلما وصفهم القرآن قال ) كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r13.claim: Its legal rulings are clear and resistant to doubt; the polygyny rule is Ibn Ashur’s example of guidance absent from Torah and Gospel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r13.anchor: وأما إن افتقدت ناحية آيات أحكامه فإنك تجدها مبرأة من اللبس وبعيدة عن تطرق الشبهة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r14.claim: The Qur’an’s clarity in law exemplifies its role as guardian over earlier scriptures, a point Ibn Ashur says he will explain at the opening of Al Imran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r14.anchor: في قوله تعالى ) وأنزلنا عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r15.claim: Al-Tanzil is the verbal noun of “send down,” applied to the revealed text because its wording descended from heaven.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p71/r15.anchor: وأما التنزيل فهو مصدر نزل ، أطلق على المنزل باعتبار أن ألفاظ القرآن أنزلت من السماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r1.claim: The verse first points to God’s power and establishes proof against unbelievers, then makes the imagery a parable for truth and falsehood, faith and disbelief, and doubt and certainty in religion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r1.anchor: صدر هذه الآية تنبيه على قدرة الله، وإقامة الحجة على الكفرة به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r2.claim: The water is rain, and wadis are depressions, trenches, or low places between mountains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r2.anchor: وقوله: أنزل من السماء ماء يريد به المطر، و «الأودية» ما بين الجبال من الانخفاض والخنادق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r3.claim: The measure may be the water allotted to each valley or the capacity of each valley according to its size.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يريد بما قدر لها من الماء، ويحتمل أن يريد بقدر ما تحتمله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r4.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r4.claim: Most read bi-qadariha with an open dāl; al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads it with a silent dāl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «بقدرها» بفتح الدال، وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي: «بقدرها» بسكون الدال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r5.claim: Zabad is the flood’s debris and the foam thrown onto its banks; a line by Hassan ibn Thabit witnesses the word.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r5.anchor: و «الزبد» ما يحمله السيل من غثاء ونحوه وما يرمي به ضفتيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r6.claim: Rābi means swollen or inflated, from the same root as rabwah, a mound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r6.anchor: و «الرابي» : المنتفخ الذي قد ربا، ومنه الربوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r7.claim: In ‘from what you heat,’ مما is the fronted predicate and زبد the subject; مثله qualifies زبد.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r7.anchor: وقوله: ومما خبر ابتداء، والابتداء قوله: زبد، ومثله نعت ل زبد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r8.claim: Materials heated for ornaments are gold and silver; utility materials include iron, lead, copper, and similar metals, whose foam resembles flood foam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r8.anchor: وهي الذهب والفضة، ابتغاء الاستمتاع بما في المرافق، وهي الحديد والرصاص والنحاس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r9.claim: Useful water and refined metal represent truth; discarded flood foam and escaping smoke represent falsehood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r9.anchor: الماء الذي تشربه الأرض من السيل فيقع النفع به هو «كالحق»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r10.speaker: مكي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r10.claim: Makki and others attach ‘in the fire’ to an omitted word meaning ‘being’ or ‘established,’ arguing that anything heated is already in the fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r10.anchor: في النار متعلق بمحذوف تقديره: كائنا أو ثابتا- كذا قال مكي وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r11.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r11.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi attaches ‘in the fire’ to ‘you heat’: an object can be heated without being in the fire, as in 28:38, where flame strikes the clay.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p307/r11.anchor: وذهب أبو علي الفارسي إلى تعلقها ب يوقدون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r1.claim: Jufāʾ is a verbal noun from a pot boiling until its foam spills out and disappears.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r1.anchor: جفاء مصدر من قولهم: أجفأت القدر إذا غلت حتى خرج زبدها وذهب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r2.speaker: رؤبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r2.claim: Ruʾba reads jufālan, from a verb meaning wind carries and scatters clouds; Abu Hatim says Bedouin readings of the Quran are not to be considered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r2.anchor: وقرأ رؤبة: «جفالا» من قولهم: جفلت الريح السحاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r3.claim: Abu Hatim says Bedouin readings of the Quran are not to be considered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r3.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: لا تعتبر قراءة الأعراب في القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r4.claim: What benefits people is the pure water and the purified useful metals or stones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r4.anchor: وقوله: ما ينفع الناس يريد الخالص من الماء ومن تلك الأحجار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Asim in Abu Bakr’s narration, Abu Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, and Hasan read with second-person tāʾ, addressing people who kindle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم- في رواية أبي بكر، وأبو جعفر والأعرج وشيبة والحسن: «توقدون» بالتاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r6.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, Hafs from Asim, Ibn Muhaysin, Mujahid, Talha, Yahya, and Kufans read with third-person yāʾ, referring to people; jufāʾ is a verbal noun used circumstantially.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم وابن محيصن ومجاهد وطلحة ويحيى وأهل الكوفة: «يوقدون» بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r7.claim: A symbolic interpretation attributed to Ibn Abbas takes the water as religious law and valleys as hearts, with the intelligent and foolish each taking their share.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: قوله تعالى: أنزل من السماء ماء يريد به الشرع والدين. وقوله: فسالت أودية: يريد به القلوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the symbolic reading is likely not soundly transmitted and follows esoteric interpretation; absent a reason, Arabic wording should retain its ordinary sense. If sound, it means truth settles in guided hearts while misgivings and doubts intrude as people study the Book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p308/r8.anchor: وهذا قول لا يصح- والله أعلم- عن ابن عباس، لأنه ينحو إلى أقوال أصحاب الرموز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya praises the Qurʾān as a divinely revealed guide that completes religion, gives promises and warnings, is easy to remember and enduring, and serves as protection, light, proof, and a universal call.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r1.anchor: أنزل إلينا القرآن العزيز، وعد فيه وبشر وأوعد وحذر، ونهى وأمر، وأكمل فيه الدين، وجعله الوسيلة الناجحة والحبل المتين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r2.claim: He says the Qurʾān’s eloquence defeats eloquent speakers, silences rhetoricians, and ennobles scholars.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r2.anchor: كلامه الذي أعجز الفصحاء، وأخرس البلغاء، وشرف العلماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r3.claim: The author says broad learning takes effort and patience, and the seeker should take a valuable share from every discipline.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r3.anchor: رأيت أن الوجه لمن تشزن للتحصيل، وعزم على الوصول، أن يأخذ من كل علم طرفا خيارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r4.claim: A specialist in a religious science should use utmost effort, explore its depths, master its principles and branches, summarize it, and answer objections.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p33/r4.anchor: أن يعتمد على علم من علوم الشرع، يستنفد فيه غاية الوسع، يجوب آفاقه، ويتتبع أعماقه، ويضبط أصوله، ويحكم فصوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r1.claim: The Qurʾān is also called the Book, the Criterion, and the Reminder.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r1.anchor: هو القرآن، وهو الكتاب، وهو الفرقان، وهو الذكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes Qurʾān as a verbal noun from qaraʾa, to recite; Abū Zayd also records the form qurʾā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r2.anchor: فالقرآن مصدر من قولك: قرأ الرجل إذا تلا يقرأ قرآنا وقراءة، وحكى أبو زيد الأنصاري: وقرءا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r3.claim: Qatāda derives Qurʾān from gathering and composing; he reads 75:17 as God’s gathering and compiling the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: «القرآن معناه التأليف قرأ الرجل إذا جمع وألف قولا» وبهذا فسر قتادة قول الله تعالى: إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r4.claim: Qatāda’s etymology is illustrated by ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm’s line about a she-camel that has not gathered a fetus in her womb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r4.anchor: قول الشاعر عمرو بن كلثوم: [الوافر] ذراعي بكرة أدماء بكر ... هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the recitation etymology, supported by Ḥassān ibn Thābit’s use of qurʾānan to mean recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r5.anchor: والقول الأول أقوى إن القرآن مصدر من قرأ إذا تلا، ومنه قول حسان بن ثابت يرثي عثمان بن عفان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r6.claim: Kitāb derives from kataba, to gather; a troop is called katība because its members are assembled.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r6.anchor: وأما الكتاب فهو مصدر من كتب إذا جمع. ومنه قيل كتيبة لاجتماعها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r7.claim: The poetic phrase write them with straps means gather them together.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r7.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: «واكتبها بأسيار» أي اجمعها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r8.claim: Furqān is a verbal noun because the Qurʾān separates truth from falsehood and believers from unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r8.anchor: وأما الفرقان أيضا فهو مصدر لأنه فرق بين الحق والباطل، والمؤمن والكافر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r9.claim: Dhikr names the Qurʾān because it reminds people of the afterlife, God, and matters they had neglected.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r9.anchor: وأما الذكر فسمي به لأنه ذكر به الناس آخرتهم وإلههم وما كانوا في غفلة عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r10.claim: Another explanation is that the Qurʾān is called the Reminder because it recounts earlier nations and prophets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r10.anchor: وقيل سمي بذلك لأنه فيه ذكر الأمم الماضية والأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r11.claim: A further explanation is that it is an honorific remembrance for Muḥammad, his people, and the scholars who know it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r11.anchor: وقيل: سمي بذلك لأنه ذكر وشرف لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وقومه وسائر العلماء به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r12.claim: Quraysh and neighboring tribes say sūra without hamza, while Tamīm and others pronounce it with hamza as suʾr or suʾra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r12.anchor: وأما السورة فإن قريشا كلها ومن جاورها من قبائل العرب كهذيل، وسعد بن بكر، وكنانة، يقولون: سورة بغير همز، وتميم كلها وغيرهم أيضا يهمزون فيقولون: سؤر وسؤرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r13.claim: With hamza, sūra is a remainder or piece from asʾara, to leave; al-Aʿshā’s line uses the verb for a wound left in the heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r13.anchor: فأما من همز فهي عنده كالبقية من الشيء والقطعة منه التي هي سؤر وسؤرة من أسأر إذا أبقى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r14.claim: Among those who omit hamza, some keep the same etymology and treat the hamza as softened.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r14.anchor: وأما من لا يهمز فمنهم من يراها من المعنى المتقدم إلا أنها سهلت همزتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r15.claim: Other non-hamza speakers derive sūra from a section of a building, since construction proceeds section by section.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r15.anchor: ومنهم من يراها مشبهة بسورة البناء أي القطعة منه، لأن كل بناء فإنما يبنى قطعة بعد قطعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r16.claim: The plural of a Qurʾānic sūra has a fatḥa on the wāw, while the plural for a building section has a sukūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p56/r16.anchor: وجمع سورة القرآن سور بفتح الواو، وجمع سورة البناء سور بسكونها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r1.claim: During the Prophet’s lifetime, people kept the Qurʾān in memory and wrote portions on sheets, palm stalks, shoulder blades, stones, and other materials.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r1.anchor: كان القرآن في مدة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متفرقا في صدور الرجال، وقد كتب الناس منه في صحف، وفي جريد، وظرر وفي لخاف وفي خزف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r2.claim: After many Qurʾān reciters died at al-Yamāma, ʿUmar advised Abū Bakr to compile the Qurʾān for fear that the senior reciters’ deaths would cause it to be lost.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r2.anchor: فلما استحر القتل بالقراء يوم اليمامة أشار عمر بن الخطاب على أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنهما بجمع القرآن، مخافة أن يموت أشياخ القراءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r3.claim: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar assigned Zayd ibn Thābit to gather the text; he completed the demanding task without arranging the sūras.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r3.anchor: فندبا إلى ذلك زيد بن ثابت فجمعه غير مرتب السور بعد تعب شديد منه رضي الله عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r4.speaker: خزيمة بن ثابت
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r4.claim: A report says the last verse of Sūrat Barāʾa was missing in the first collection and found with Khuzayma; al-Ṭabarī places the loss in the later collection, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the earlier account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r4.anchor: وروي أن في هذا الجمع سقطت الآية من آخر براءة حتى وجدها عند خزيمة بن ثابت. وحكى الطبري أنه إنما سقطت له في الجمع الأخير، والأول أصح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r5.speaker: البخاري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r5.claim: Al-Bukhārī’s version names Abū Khuzayma al-Anṣārī as the person with whom the verse was found.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r5.anchor: وهو الذي حكى البخاري إلا أنه قال فيه مع أبي خزيمة الأنصاري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r6.speaker: البخاري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r6.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports that a verse from al-Aḥzāb, Among the believers are men, was missing in the second compilation until Zayd found it with Khuzayma ibn Thābit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r6.anchor: وقال: إن في الجمع الثاني فقد زيد آية من سورة الأحزاب من المؤمنين رجال [الأحزاب: 33] فوجدها مع خزيمة بن ثابت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r7.claim: The sheets passed from Abū Bakr to ʿUmar and then Ḥafṣa; meanwhile regional Companion codices differed in line with the seven aḥruf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r7.anchor: وبقيت الصحف عند أبي بكر، ثم عند عمر بن الخطاب بعده، ثم عند حفصة بنته في خلافة عثمان، وانتشرت في خلال ذلك صحف في الآفاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r8.speaker: البخاري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r8.claim: Al-Bukhārī names three Qurayshī scribes who assisted Zayd for ʿUthmān: Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r8.anchor: وقرن بزيد فيما ذكر البخاري ثلاثة من قريش: سعيد بن العاصي، وعبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام، وعبد الله بن الزبير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r9.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says that only Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ assisted Zayd; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this report weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r9.anchor: وقال الطبري فيما روي: إنه قرن بزيد أبان بن سعيد بن العاصي وحده، وهذا ضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r10.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Ḥafṣa’s sheets served as the master copy in the final collection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r10.anchor: وقال الطبري أيضا: إن الصحف التي كانت عند حفصة جعلت إماما في هذا الجمع الأخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r11.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r11.claim: ʿUthmān told the scribes to use Quraysh’s language if they differed; they chose tāʾ in al-tābūt over Zayd’s hāʾ reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r11.anchor: وروي أن عثمان رضي الله عنه قال لهم: «إذا اختلفتم في شيء فاجعلوه بلغة قريش»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r12.claim: In the variant al-tābūt/al-tābūh, Zayd ibn Thābit read with hāʾ and the Qurayshīs with tāʾ, so the codex adopted tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r12.anchor: فاختلفوا في التابوه والتابوت، قرأه زيد بن ثابت بالهاء والقرشيون بالتاء، فأثبته بالتاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r13.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r13.claim: ʿUthmān produced codex copies for the regions and ordered the remaining codices burned or torn; an alternate transmission says buried, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the first reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p49/r13.anchor: وكتب المصحف على ما هو عليه غابر الدهر ونسخ عثمان منه نسخا ووجه بها إلى الآفاق، وأمر بما سواها من المصاحف أن تحرق أو تخرق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r1.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( أنزل من السماء ماء ) يعني المطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r2.claim: Awdiya is the plural of wādin, a low passage between two mountains where rainwater gathers and flows.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r2.anchor: وهي جمع واد وهو كل منفرج بين جبلين يجتمع إليه ماء المطر فيسيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r3.claim: Each valley carries water according to its capacity: a small valley carries little, and a broad one carries much.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r3.anchor: أي بمبلغ ما تحمل فإن صغر الوادي قل الماء وإن هو اتسع كثر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r4.speaker: الحسن وابن جبير وأبو العالية وأيوب وابن يعمر وأبو حاتم عن يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ayyūb, Ibn Yaʿmar, and Abū Ḥātim from Yaʿqūb read bi-qadrihā with a still dāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن جبير وأبو العالية وايوب وابن يعمر وأبو حاتم عن يعقوب بقدرها باسكان الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r5.claim: The wording expands the expression by omitting the genitive nouns: the valleys' waters flowed and the water flowed according to its measure.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r5.anchor: وقوله فسالت أودية توسع في الكلام والمعنى سالت مياهها فحذف المضاف وكذلك قوله بقدرها أي بقدر مياهها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r6.claim: The foam is high, rising above the water.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r6.anchor: ( فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ) أي عاليا فوق الماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read the verb in the second person, tuqidūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r8.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read the verb in the third person, yuqidūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r9.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the second-person reading follows the preceding address, though it can also address all people generally; the third-person reading follows earlier mention of absent parties.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي من قرأ بالتاء فلما قبله من الخطاب وهو قوله أفاتخذتم ويجوز أن يكون خطابا عاما للكافة ومن قرأ بالياء فلأن ذكر الغيبة قد تقدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r10.claim: The material put into the fire is melted ore or precious material.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r10.anchor: ويعني بقوله ( ومما توقدون عليه ) ما يدخل إلى النار فيذاب من الجواهر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r11.claim: The jewelry sought from the molten material is gold and silver.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r12.claim: The useful goods include iron, brass, copper, and lead, made into vessels and other useful things.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r12.anchor: ( أو متاع ) يعني الحديد والصفر والنحاس والرصاص تتخذ منه الأواني والأشياء التي ينتفع بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r13.claim: Like floodwater, molten metal produces foam; this is a second simile.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r13.anchor: ( زبد مثله ) أي له زبد إذا أذيب مثل زبد السيل فهذا مثل آخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r14.claim: One view maps the water and valleys onto the Qur'an and human hearts, which receive according to faith, doubt, intelligence, and ignorance; believers benefit while unbelievers do not.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r14.anchor: أحدها أنه القرآن شبه نزوله من السماء بالماء وشبه قلوب العباد بالأودية تحمل منه على قدر اليقين والشك والعقل والجهل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r15.claim: A second view maps the lasting clear water to truth and the vanishing foam to falsehood, which God will abolish even if it temporarily rises above truth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p321/r15.anchor: والثاني أنه الحق والباطل فالحق شبه بالماء الباقي الصافي والباطل مشبه بالزبد الذاهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r1.claim: A third view compares the believer's belief and deeds to useful water, and the unbeliever's belief and deeds to foam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r1.anchor: والثالث أنه مثل ضربه الله للمؤمن والكافر فمثل المؤمن واعتقاده وعمله كالماء المنتفع به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r2.claim: Just as in the preceding example, God gives a likeness of truth and falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ( كذلك ) أي كما ذكر هذا يضرب الله مثل الحق والباطل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses it as God making both truth and falsehood into examples.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة كذلك يمثل الله الحق ويمثل الباطل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says jufāʾ is what a valley casts onto its banks; the verb is also used of a pot throwing off its foam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r4.anchor: فأما الجفاء فقال ابن قتيبة هو ما رمى به الوادي إلى جنباته يقال أجفأت القدر بزبدها إذا ألقته عنها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r5.claim: Ibn Fāris defines jufāʾ as what a flood casts away and notes that the word derives from the root for repudiation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r5.anchor: قال ابن فارس الجفاء ما نفاه السيل ومنه اشتقاق الجفاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī glosses jufāʾ as decayed and scattered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري جفاء أي باليا متفرقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the foam amounts to nothing when touched.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس إذا مس الزبد لم يكن شيئا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r8.claim: What benefits people is the water and useful metals after their foam has gone; it remains in the earth and benefits them, just as truth endures for its people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p322/r8.anchor: ( وأما ما ينفع الناس ) من الماء والجواهر التي زال زبدها ( فيمكث في الأرض ) فينتفع به ( كذلك ) يبقى الحق لأهله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r1.claim: The verse gives two comparisons: truth persists, while falsehood dwindles and disappears.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r1.anchor: اشتملت هذه الآية الكريمة على مثلين مضروبين للحق في ثباته وبقائه، والباطل في اضمحلاله وفنائه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r2.claim: Rain fills each valley according to its size; this represents hearts’ differing capacities, some able to receive much knowledge and others little.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r2.anchor: فهذا كبير وسع كثيرا من الماء، وهذا صغير فوسع بقدره،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r3.claim: The flood carries raised foam across the surface of the water, an image for falsehood that will not endure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r3.anchor: {فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا} أي: فجاء على وجه الماء الذي سال في هذه الأودية زبد عال عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r4.claim: The second image is metal smelted in fire to make gold or silver jewelry, or copper and iron implements; smelting also produces surface slag.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r4.anchor: {ومما يوقدون عليه في النار} هذا هو المثل الثاني، وهو ما يسبك في النار من ذهب أو فضة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r5.claim: When truth and falsehood meet, falsehood has no permanence, just as water foam and metal slag disappear; useless foam disperses along the valley and onto trees, then wind scatters it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r5.anchor: {كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل} أي: إذا اجتمعا لا ثبات للباطل ولا دوام له، كما أن الزبد لا يثبت مع الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r6.claim: What benefits people remains: the water and useful metal endure, just as truth lasts; the verse’s parables are for reflection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r6.anchor: أي: لا ينتفع به، بل يتفرق ويتمزق ويذهب في جانبي الوادي،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir cites the declaration that God gives these parables for people, which only the learned understand; one early Muslim said he would weep if he failed to understand a Quranic parable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r7.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون} [العنكبوت: 43] . قال بعض السلف:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the valleys signify hearts receiving according to their certainty or doubt: doubt does not benefit its practitioner, while certainty benefits its people; the foam is doubt and enduring benefit is certainty, as smelting separates pure metal from impurity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p447/r8.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: قوله تعالى: {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها} هذا مثل ضربه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r1.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas’s explanation that the flood carries wood and debris from the valley; gold and silver are useful, while copper and iron produce slag, and water benefits the land by making it grow.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r1.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس قوله: {أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا} يقول: احتمل السيل ما في الوادي من عود ودمنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas compares lasting benefit to righteous deeds and fading slag to evil deeds; guidance and truth from God endure for those who act by them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r2.anchor: فجعل ذاك (3) مثل العمل الصالح يبقى لأهله، والعمل السيئ يضمحل عن أهله، كما يذهب هذا الزبد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r3.claim: Iron must be heated to burn away its impurity and retain sound material for a knife or sword; likewise falsehood vanishes at resurrection when deeds are displayed, and the people of truth benefit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r3.anchor: كذلك الحديد لا يستطاع أن يعمل منه سكين ولا سيف حتى يدخل في النار فتأكل خبثه، ويخرج جيده فينتفع به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r4.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن البصري، عطاء، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r4.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ata, Qatada, and other early and later authorities are also reported to have explained this parable in this way.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r4.anchor: وكذلك روي في تفسيرها عن مجاهد، والحسن البصري، وعطاء، وقتادة، وغير واحد من السلف والخلف.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r5.claim: The water and fire parables are compared with the two images for hypocrites at the start of al-Baqara: a fire and a rainstorm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r5.anchor: وقد ضرب الله، سبحانه وتعالى، في أول سورة البقرة للمنافقين مثلين ناريا ومائيا، وهما قوله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r6.claim: The two examples for disbelievers in al-Nur are a mirage and darkness at sea; a hadith in both Sahih collections depicts Jews at resurrection asking for water and being led toward a fire that looks like a crushing mirage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r6.anchor: وهكذا ضرب للكافرين في سورة النور مثلين، أحدهما: قوله: {والذين كفروا أعمالهم كسراب بقيعة يحسبه الظمآن ماء}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r7.claim: A hadith in both Sahih collections says the Jews will plead for water at resurrection and be shown a fire that appears as a mirage and crushes itself together.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r7.anchor: فيقال لليهود يوم القيامة: فما تريدون؟ فيقولون: أي ربنا، عطشنا فاسقنا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r8.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r8.claim: In the rain parable, some soil absorbs rain and grows vegetation, some holds water that benefits people, and barren soil does neither; these are those who learn and teach the Prophet’s guidance, preserve it for others, and reject it. The report is in both Sahih collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p448/r8.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن مثل ما بعثني الله به من الهدى والعلم، كمثل غيث أصاب أرضا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p449/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p449/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p449/r1.claim: The Prophet compares himself and his community to a man lighting a fire as moths and other creatures rush into it; he tries to restrain them from the Fire, but they overcome him and leap in. Both Sahih collections transmit the parable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p449/r1.anchor: هذا ما حدثنا أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "مثلي ومثلكم، كمثل رجل استوقد نارا، فلما أضاءت ما حوله

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r1.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read يوقدون with ya; Abu Ubayd prefers this because ينفع الناس follows and the passage has no direct address.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: (يوقدون) بالياء، واختاره أبو عبيد لقوله: ينفع الناس، قال: ولا مخاطبة هاهنا

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r2.claim: The remaining readers use ta, addressing the audience.

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r3.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r3.claim: The readers have بقدرها with fatḥa on the dal; Hasan is also reported with the dal lightened.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r3.anchor: وقراءة القراء: (بقدرها) بفتح الدال، وعن الحسن بقدرها مخففة.

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r4.claim: Sayl is the verbal noun for water or something else flowing, and also names the water itself because it runs down from higher places.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r4.anchor: السيل: مصدر سال الماء وغيره يسيل سيلا، والسيل: الماء أيضا سمي لسيلانه وجريه من مواضع مرتفعة

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r5.claim: A wadi is the low slope or hollow of a great mountain where rain gathers; its plurals are irregular, and Jarir's line witnesses the form الأوداه.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r5.anchor: والوادي: سفح الجبل العظيم المنخفض الذي يجتمع فيه المطر، ويقال: واد وأودية على غير قياس، وقد جمع أوداه، قال جرير: عرفت ببرقة الأوداه رسما

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r6.claim: The verb ودى الوادي means the valley flowed; diya is named for the great wealth collected to pay compensation for a slain person, and ودى also means to pay that compensation.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r6.anchor: ويقال: ودى الوادي يدي إذا سال، ومنه: أخذت الدية؛ لأنه جمع المال العظيم الذي يودى عن القتيل

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r7.claim: Zabad is the scum or froth that rises over a boiling pot, sea, or flood.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r7.anchor: والزبد: زبد القدر، وزبد البحر، وزبد السيل، وهو الخبث الذي يعلوه عند الغليان.

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r8.claim: Rabi means increased or grown; the root conveys increase, as in commercial usury.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r8.anchor: والربا: أصله الزيادة، ومنه الربا في البيع، والرابي الزائد

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r9.claim: Jufaa is what a flood casts away in its channel; the related verbs describe a valley casting out debris or a pot releasing foam, and it can mean a land's good disappearing.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r9.anchor: والجفاء: ما جفاه السيل في مجراه، يقال: جفى الوادي وأجفاه إذا ألقى غثاءه، وأجفأت القدر: ألقت زبدها

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r10.speaker: القتبي
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r10.claim: Al-Qutbi defines jufaa as material a valley throws to its banks.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r10.anchor: قال [القتبي]: الجفاء ما رماه الوادي إلى جنباته

JISHUMI:v5p3775/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r11.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says a wind is said to disperse a cloud, and explains jufaa as what a flood rejects.
JISHUMI:v5p3775/r11.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: يقال: جفأت الريح السحاب: فرقته، والجفاء مشتق من الجفاء، وهو ما نفاه السيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r1.claim: This parable contrasts truth and its people with falsehood and its faction, as the previous verse compared them to sight and blindness, light and darkness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r1.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله للحق وأهله والباطل وحزبه ، كما ضرب الأعمى والبصير والظلمات والنور مثلا لهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r2.claim: Truth is like rain that fills people's valleys, revives them, and benefits them, and like useful metals fashioned into ornaments, vessels, and tools; iron alone is valuable for its strength.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r2.anchor: فمثل الحق وأهله بالماء الذي ينزله من السماء فتسيل به أودية الناس فيحيون به وينفعهم أنواع المنافع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r3.claim: Falsehood quickly vanishes and sheds any usefulness like flood foam and the dross floating above molten metal; water and metals remain and their benefits endure.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r3.anchor: وشبه الباطل في سرعة اضمحلاله ووشك زواله وانسلاخه عن المنفعة ، بزبد السيل الذي يرمي به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r4.claim: The valleys are indefinite because rainfall alternates among regions, so only some valleys flow at any given time.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r4.anchor: لأن المطر لا يأتي إلا على طريق المناوبة بين البقاع ، فيسيل بعض أودية الأرض دون بعض .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r5.claim: Each valley receives the amount God knows will benefit those rained upon without harming them; the analogy requires pure beneficial rain, unlike destructive floods.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r5.anchor: بمقدارها الذي عرف الله أنه نافع للممطور عليهم غير ضار . ألا ترى إلى قوله : { وأما ما ينفع الناس }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r6.claim: Mentioning ornaments and goods explains how both water and metal benefit people, specifying metal's uses beneath the general statement that what benefits people remains.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r6.anchor: الفائدة فيه كالفائدة في قوله : { بقدرها } لأنه جمع الماء والفلز في النفع في قوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r7.claim: The phrase comprehensively covers kinds of metal while displaying grandeur by seeming to treat metal as insignificant, as kings do; compare 28:38.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r7.anchor: عبارة جامعة لأنواع الفلز ، مع إظهار الكبرياء في ذكره على وجه التهاون به كما هو هجيرى الملوك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r8.claim: من may mark the starting point, with dross arising from metal, or partitive sense, with some of it becoming swollen foam atop the flood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r8.anchor: و ( من ) لابتداء الغاية . أي : ومنه ينشأ زبد مثل زبد الماء . أو للتبعيض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r9.claim: The word evokes the pot casting off its foam and the flood sweeping it away; the author gives related forms أجفأ and أجفل.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r9.anchor: وجفأت القدر بزبدها ، وأجفأ السيل وأجفل .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r10.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r10.claim: Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjaj has a reading جفالا; Abu Hatim objects to accepting it because Ruʾba ate mice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r10.anchor: وفي قراءة رؤبة ابن العجاج : جفالا وعن أبي حاتم : لا يقرأ بقراءة رؤبة ، لأنه كان يأكل الفأر .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r11.claim: A variant reads يوقدون in the third person, meaning people kindle the fire.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p493/r11.anchor: وقرىء : ( يوقدون ) ، بالياء : أي يوقد الناس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r1.claim: One explanation is that each valley receives water according to what was allotted to it, whether little or much.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r1.anchor: يعني بما قدر لها من قليل أو كثير

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r2.claim: Alternatively, small valleys flow in proportion to their smallness and large valleys to their size.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r2.anchor: الصغير من الأودية سال بقدر صغره , والكبير منها سال بقدر كبره

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r3.claim: Rain images the Qur’an’s universal good and lasting benefit; valleys are hearts that receive according to their capacity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r3.anchor: فشبه القرآن بالمطر لعموم خيره وبقاء نفعه , وشبه القلوب بالأودية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the water is the Qur’an and the valleys are people’s hearts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { أنزل من السماء ماء } أي قرآنا { فسالت أودية بقدرها } قال : الأودية قلوب العباد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r6.claim: Useful water that remains represents truth; foam that vanishes without benefit represents falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r6.anchor: فالحق ممثل بالماء الذي يبقى في الأرض فينتفع به , والباطل ممثل بالزبد الذي يذهب جفاء لا ينتفع به

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r7.claim: The adornment sought by heating metal means gold and silver.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r8.claim: The metal made for use means brass and copper.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r9.claim: Smelting produces dross like water’s foam: useless impurity departs as falsehood does, while the refined remainder is useful like truth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r9.anchor: إذا سبك بالنار كان له خبث كالزبد الذي على الماء يذهب فلا ينتفع به كالباطل , ويبقى صفوة فينتفع به كالحق

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r10.speaker: ابن جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r10.claim: Ibn Jarīr glosses jufāʾ as separated or dispersed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r11.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā glosses it as cast away onto the earth’s surface.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r11.anchor: جافيا على وجه الأرض , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r12.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r12.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses it as thrown away.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r13.speaker: رؤية
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayda heard Ruʾya read jafālan; he explains ajfalat al-qidr as the pot casting out its foam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p105/r13.anchor: سمع رؤية يقرأ : جفالا . قال أبو عبيدة : يقال أجفلت القدر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: A second etymology derives Quran from qara'a meaning to gather and join together, since its verses are collected; Qatada’s poetry compares this with a womb gathering a child.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor: وهو قول قتادة ، أنه مصدر من قولك قرأت الشيء ، إذا جمعته وضممت بعضه إلى بعض

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum’s verse uses qara'at for a womb that has not gathered a child, supporting the gathering etymology.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: كما قال عمرو بن كلثوم : تريك إذا دخلت على خلاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: Furqan names the Quran because God separates truth from falsehood; this is the consensus, since the root means separation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: فلأن الله عز وجل فرق بين الحق والباطل ، وهو قول الجماعة ، لأن أصل الفرقان هو الفرق بين شيئين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: Kitab derives from writing or gathering letters together; it is called a book even when already written.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: فلأنه مصدر من قولك كتبت كتابا ، والكتاب هو خط الكاتب حروف المعجم مجموعة ومتفرقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r5.claim: Dhikr may mean a reminder from God teaching servants duties and limits, or honor and renown for believers; the latter is linked to 43:44.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r5.anchor: حدوده . والثاني : أنه ذكر وشرف وفخر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r6.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r6.claim: Al-Farra derives Torah from the expression for a firebrand giving off fire, so the name means illumination.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r6.anchor: فإن الفراء يجعلها مشتقة من قولهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r7.claim: Zabur derives from the verb for writing a book; a poet compares the image of dwellings to a written mark.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r7.anchor: وأما الزبور ، فإنه مشتق من قولهم : زبر الكتاب يزبره إذا كتبه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r8.claim: Injil derives from extracting something, as a man’s offspring are called his extracted progeny; a poem illustrates the usage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p24/r8.anchor: فهو مأخوذ من نجلت الشيء ، إذا أخرجته

MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r1.claim: The rain fills each valley to the amount it can hold.
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها ﴾ يعني ملأها ما أطاقت

MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r2.claim: The foam is the froth carried along by the flood.
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r2.anchor: يعني ملأها ما أطاقت ﴿ فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ﴾ والزبد الذي في السيل ثم استقبل فقال

MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r3.claim: The sought-after metal goods are iron, copper, and lead.
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r3.anchor: ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع ﴾ فالمتاع الحديد والنحاس والرصاص

MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r4.claim: The metalworking foam is the dross, corresponding to flood foam; it goes away as sediment, while the beneficial water remains on earth, illustrating truth and falsehood.
MUJAHID:v1p327#2/r4.anchor: وأما ﴿ زبد مثله ﴾ فخبث ذلك وهو مثله مثل الزبد فيذهب

MUQATIL:13:17-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r1.claim: The parable contrasts disbelief and faith, truth and falsehood: rainwater represents the Quran taught to believers and abandoned by disbelievers; valleys carry water according to their size.
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r1.anchor: ضرب الله مثل الكفر والإيمان، ومثل الحق والباطل

MUQATIL:13:17-18/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r2.claim: The flood carries foam that rises high.
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r2.anchor: فاحتمل السيل } ، يعني سيل الماء، { زبدا رابيا } ، يعني عاليا

MUQATIL:13:17-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r3.claim: The jewelry sought from fire is gold and silver; utensils and goods include brass, iron, and lead, which also produce foam when heated.

MUQATIL:13:17-18/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r4.claim: Foam from the flood is useless, and heating jewelry or goods expels the useless impurities while the useful metals remain.
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r4.anchor: فالسيل زبد لا ينتفع به، والحلي والمتاع له أيضا زبد

MUQATIL:13:17-18/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r5.claim: Water represents Quranic truth, valleys hearts, and the flood desires; useful water and purified metal represent truth that benefits its people in the Hereafter, while foam and slag represent useless falsehood.
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r5.anchor: ومثل الماء مثل القرآن، وهو الحق، ومثل الأودية مثل القلوب

MUQATIL:13:17-18/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r6.claim: Jufāʾ means dried up and useless, like foam that benefits people not at all.
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r6.anchor: يعني يابسا لا ينتفع به الناس كما لا ينتفع بالسيل

MUQATIL:13:17-18/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r7.claim: Useful water remains for drinking and irrigation, just as useful truth remains and benefits its people; God sets forth likenesses in these three examples together.
MUQATIL:13:17-18/r7.anchor: فيستقون ويزرعون عليه وينتفعون به، يقول: { كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r1.claim: The one who sent down water is God, the One, the Conqueror; the sky here means clouds and water means rain.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r1.anchor: ﴿ أنزل ﴾ اي الواحد القهار وهو الله سبحانه ﴿ من السماء ﴾ من السحاب ﴿ ماء ﴾ مطرا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r2.claim: A wadi is a place where abundant water flows; the plural is indefinite because rain alternates among lands, so only some valleys flow at a time.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r2.anchor: جمع واد وهو الموضع الذي يسيل فيه الماء بكثرة وإنما نكر لأن المطر لا يأتي إلا على طريق المناوبة بين البقاع

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r3.claim: Each valley receives the amount God knows will benefit those rained upon without harming them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r3.anchor: بمقدارها الذي علم الله أنه نافع للممطور عليهم غير ضار

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r4.claim: The flood lifts froth on the water; the foam rises and swells above it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r4.anchor: ﴿ فاحتمل السيل ﴾ اي رفع ﴿ زبدا ﴾ هو ما علا وجه الماء من الرغوة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r5.claim: Kufans other than Abū Bakr read the verb with yāʾ; min can mark origin of the foam or partitive division.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r5.anchor: وبالياء كوفي غير أبي بكر ومن لابتداء الغاية أى ومنه ينشأ زبد مثل زبد الماء أو للتبعيض أي وبعضه زبد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r6.claim: “In the fire” is circumstantial to the pronoun in “upon it”; “seeking adornment” is a circumstantial verbal noun describing the burners.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r6.anchor: ﴿ في النار ﴾ حال من الضمير في عليه أي ومما توقدون عليه ثابتا في النار ﴿ ابتغاء حلية ﴾ مبتغين حلية

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r7.claim: The useful goods include vessels and travel or home implements made from iron, copper, and lead; the phrase coordinates with adornment, jewelry of gold and silver.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r7.anchor: من الحديد والنحاس والرصاص يتخذ منها الأوانى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r8.claim: Zabad is a nominative subject, mithluhu qualifies it, and the phrase “from what you heat” is its predicate: molten metals produce foam like water.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r8.anchor: نعت له ومما توقدون خبر له أي لهذه الفلزات

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r9.claim: Jufāʾan means dissipating; it is what a boiling pot or surging sea casts away, from a root meaning to cast down.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r9.anchor: حال اي متلاشيا وهو ما تقذفه القدر عند الغليان والبحر عند الطغيان والجفء الرمى وجفوت الرجل صرعته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r10.claim: Useful water remains in springs, wells, grains, and fruits, while metals and gems remain in the earth for a long time.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r11.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r11.claim: A general allegory compares beneficial, enduring water and metals with truth and its people, and transient foam with falsehood and its faction.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r11.anchor: قيل هذا مثل ضربه الله للحق وأهله والباطل وحزبه فمثل الحق واهله بالماء الذي ينزل من السماء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r12.speaker: الجمهور
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r12.claim: The majority's inward analogy makes rain the Quran, valleys hearts of differing capacity, foam the ego and Satan's whispers, and clear water lasting truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r12.anchor: قال الجمهور وهذا مثل قوله الله تعالى للقرآن والقلوب والحق والباطل فالماء القرآن نزل لحياة الجنان كالماء للابدان والأودية للقلوب ومعنى بقدرها بقدر سعة القلب وضيقه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r13.speaker: الجمهور
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r13.claim: Gold and silver adornment represents noble states and morals, useful metal goods sincere deeds for salvation, and foam ostentation, defects, boredom, and laziness.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p214/r13.anchor: واما حلية الذهب والفضة فمثل للاحوال السنية والأخلاق الزكية

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r1.claim: The first parable likens disbelief to foam riding water: it vanishes, clings to the valley sides, and is blown away, just as disbelief perishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r1.anchor: ضرب مثلا للحق والباطل فشبه الكفر بالزبد الذي يعلو الماء، فإنه يضمحل

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the valleys flowed according to how full they were.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: «فسالت أودية بقدرها» قال: بقدر ملئها

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says flow was according to each valley's small or large size.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: بقدر صغرها وكبرها

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r4.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r4.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī and al-Ḥasan read bi-qadrihā with a still dāl; the meaning is the same.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي والحسن «بقدرها» بسكون الدال، والمعنى واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r5.claim: Another interpretation is according to what had been apportioned for the valleys.

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r6.claim: A valley is called wādin because it emerges and flows; wādin here can refer to flowing water itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r6.anchor: والأودية جمع الوادي وسمي واديا لخروجه وسيلانه

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r7.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī calls the valleys flowing an expansive expression with water omitted; by their measure means their water volume, since valleys do not flow according to themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: «فسالت أودية» توسع أي سال ماؤها فحذف

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r8.claim: Rābiyan describes foam rising high above the water; Mujāhid says the phrase completes the first parable.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r8.anchor: أي طالعا عاليا مرتفعا فوق الماء، وتم الكلام قاله مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r9.claim: The second parable concerns material heated to obtain gold or silver jewelry, or useful metal goods.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r9.anchor: { ابتغاء حلية } أي حلية الذهب والفضة

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r10.claim: Mujāhid identifies useful materials as iron, copper, and lead.

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r11.claim: Smelted metals also produce foam: minerals mixed with earth are heated so the soil separates, just as mixed soil produces torrent foam.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r11.anchor: وإنما احتمل السيل الزبد لأن الماء خالطه تراب الأرض فصار ذلك زبدا

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r12.claim: Mujāhid interprets jufāʾ as solid or congealed.

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r13.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ says a boiling pot ejects its foam or the foam solidifies at the bottom; jufāʾ is also what a valley casts away.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r13.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: أجفأت القدر إذا غلت حتى ينصب زبدها

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r14.speaker: رؤبة
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reports hearing Ruʾba read jafālan; related verbs mean a pot casts foam or wind parts clouds.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r14.anchor: وحكى أبو عبيدة أنه سمع رؤبة يقرأ «جفالا»

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r15.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r15.claim: Mujāhid says what benefits people and remains is pure, clear water.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r15.anchor: قال مجاهد: هو الماء الخالص الصافي

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r16.claim: Another interpretation includes water and purified gold, silver, iron, copper, and lead; the parables show truth enduring while falsehood, though temporarily dominant, perishes like foam.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r16.anchor: وقيل: الماء وما خلص من الذهب والفضة والحديد والنحاس والرصاص

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r17.claim: An alternative parable likens the Qur'an to beneficial, enduring rain and people's hearts to valleys that receive it according to capacity.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r17.anchor: وقيل: المراد مثل ضربه الله للقرآن وما يدخل منه القلوب فشبه القرآن بالمطر

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the water as the Qur'an and the valleys as servants' hearts.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r18.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «أنزل من السماء ماء» قال: قرآنا

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r19.speaker: صاحب سوق العروس
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r19.claim: Ṣāḥib Suq al-ʿArūs says, if this reading is sound, clear water represents the Qur'an, valleys hearts, firm verses clear water, and ambiguous verses foam.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r19.anchor: قال صاحب «سوق العروس» إن صح هذا التفسير فالمعنى فيه أن الله سبحانه مثل القرآن بالماء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r20.claim: Another symbolic reading makes the foam illusions of the self and dangers of doubt rising and agitating over the pure current.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17/r20.anchor: وقيل: الزبد مخايل النفس وغوائل الشك ترتفع من حيث ما فيها فتضطرب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r1.claim: In the spiritual parable, jewelry represents elevated states and virtuous character that beautify people and support good works, as precious metals adorn women and give things value.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r1.anchor: والأخلاق الزكية التي بها جمال الرجال، وقوام صالح الأعمال، كما أن من الذهب والفضة زينة النساء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r2.speaker: حميد وابن محيصن ويحيى والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وحفص
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r2.claim: Ḥumayd, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read the verb in third person; Abū ʿUbayd prefers it because ينفع الناس is also third person and there is no address here.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r2.anchor: وقرأ حميد وابن محيصن ويحيى والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وحفص «يوقدون» بالياء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r3.claim: The remaining readers use the second-person reading, matching the earlier address about taking protectors besides God.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r3.anchor: الباقون بالتاء لقوله في أول الكلام: «أفاتخذتم من دونه أولياء»

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r4.claim: Fī al-nār modifies an omitted circumstantial participle describing what is heated; the pronoun in عليه is its referent.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r4.anchor: وقوله: «في النار» متعلق بمحذوف، وهو في موضع الحال، وذو الحال الهاء التي في «عليه»

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r5.speaker: author
