QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r5.claim: It cannot attach directly to يوقدون, since what is heated is necessarily in the fire and the phrase would add no information.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r5.anchor: ولا يستقيم أن يتعلق «في النار» ب«يوقدون» من حيث لا يستقيم أوقدت عليه في النار

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r6.claim: Ibtighāʾa ḥilyatin is an object expressing purpose.

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r7.claim: One parse makes zabadun the subject and mithluhu its predicate, meaning foam like the torrent's foam.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r7.anchor: «زبد مثله» ابتداء وخبر أي زبد مثل زبد السيل

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r8.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī instead makes zabadun the subject, mithluhu its modifier, and the preceding phrase its predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r8.anchor: الكسائي: «زبد» ابتداء، و«مثله» نعت له، والخبر في الجملة التي قبله

QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r9.claim: Just as He clarified these examples, God makes other parables clear; this completes the sentence before the next verse begins.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:17-18/r9.anchor: أي كما بين لكم هذه الأمثال فكذلك يضربها بينات. تم الكلام

BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r1.claim: Useful water and refined metal remain and benefit people: water gathers in useful places or seeps to springs, channels, and wells, while metal lasts a long time.
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r1.anchor: فيمكث في الأرض أي يبقى ولا يذهب فينتفع به الناس

BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r2.claim: God uses parables to clarify obscure matters; representation effectively teaches the ignorant by presenting the unfamiliar in a familiar form.
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r2.anchor: يضرب الله الأمثال ويبينها لإيضاح المشتبهات ، والمثل القول الدائر بين الناس

BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashifi reads the water as Qur'an that gives life to believers' hearts, valleys as hearts receiving according to capacity, and foam as egoistic thoughts and satanic whispers.
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r3.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (بعضي بادنندكه مراد ازين آب قر آنست كه حيات دل اهل ايمانست وأودية دلها اندكه فراخور استعداد خود ازان فيض ميكيرند

BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r4.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Layth likens falsehood to weightless, unrewarded foam carried by desire; faith and certainty benefit their people in the afterlife like clear water benefits people here, while disbelief and doubt benefit neither world.
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الليث في تفسيره شبه الباطل بالزبد يعني احتملت القلوب على قدر هواها باطلا كثيرا فكما أن السيل يجمع كل قذر فكذلك الهوى يحتمل الباطل

BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r5.claim: The Sufi commentary gives three levels: love waters souls, beauty's lights water hearts, and divine self-disclosure waters secrets; each bears foam of animal traits, spiritual selfhood, or metaphorical existence.
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r5.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية انزل من السماء من سماء القلوب ماء المحبة فسالت أوية النفوس بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا

BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r6.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r6.claim: The Mathnawi says manifestation of eternal qualities burns away transient, created qualities.
BURSEVI:v4p236#2/r6.anchor:
قال في المثنوى :
ون تجلى كرد اوصاف قديم
س بسوزد وصف حادث را كليم

RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r1.claim: Rainwater settles in low valleys according to their capacity; excess spreads across the land, while the foam it carries rises and disperses at the edges, leaving the water behind.
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r1.anchor: ومن حق الماء أن يستقر في الأودية المنخفضة عن الجبال والتلال بمقدار سعة تلك الأودية وصغرها

RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r2.claim: When the seven metals are melted for jewelry or useful utensils, their dross separates and vanishes while the pure, useful substance remains.
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r2.anchor: كل واحد من الأجساد السبعة إذا أذيب بالنار لابتغاء حلية أو متاع آخر من الأمتعة التي يحتاج إليها

RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r3.claim: The water from the sky is the Qurʾān and the valleys are hearts, which receive its light according to purity and understanding; doubts mingle with its proofs but finally vanish, leaving knowledge, religion, wisdom, and unveiling.
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r3.anchor: أنزل من سماء الكبرياء والجلالة والإحسان ماء وهو القرآن ، والأودية قلوب العباد

RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r4.claim: Rāzī observes that most commentators did not explain how the likeness maps onto what it represents.
RAZI-FULL:v19p28/r4.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين سكتوا عن بيان كيفية التمثيل والتشبيه

RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r1.speaker: عامة أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r1.claim: The majority of lexicographers define a wādī as a low open tract between mountains and hills through which a torrent runs.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r1.anchor: القول الأول : أنه عبارة عن الفضاء المنخفض عن الجبال والتلال الذي يجري فيه السيل ، هذا قول عامة أهل اللغة

RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r2.speaker: السهروردي
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r2.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says wādī can mean flowing water itself, so the phrase is figurative: the waters of the valleys flowed, with the annexed noun standing for the omitted one.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r2.anchor: القول الثاني : قال السهروردي يسمى الماء واديا إذا سال

RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī explains the unusual wādin/awdiya plural by the overlap of fāʿil and faʿīl, whose regular plural patterns cross over; he gives further parallel forms.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي رحمه الله : الأودية جمع واد ولا نعلم فاعلا جمع على أفعلة قال : ويشبه أن يكون ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r4.speaker: غيره
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r4.claim: Another grammarian offers nād/andiyah, ‘meeting place/meeting places,’ as a parallel to wādī/awdiya.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r4.anchor: وقال غيره : نظير واد وأودية ، ناد وأندية للمجالس

RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r5.claim: The indefinite plural signals that rainfall alternates among regions, so some valleys flow while others do not.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r5.anchor: إنما ذكر لفظ أودية على سبيل التنكير ، لأن المطر لا يأتي إلا على طريق المناوبة بين البقاع

RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r6.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r6.claim: Al-Wāḥidī glosses qadr and qadar as an amount or measure, such as the weight of a quantity of coins.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r6.anchor: قال الواحدي : القدر والقدر مبلغ الشيء يقال كم قدر هذه الدراهم وكم قدرها ومقدارها ؟

RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r7.claim: The amount of water corresponds to the valley’s size: a small valley carries little, and a broad one carries much.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29/r7.anchor: بقدرها } أي من الماء ، فإن صغر الوادي قل الماء

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ notes the verb azbada, ‘to foam,’ and says zabad is the noun for foam.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r1.anchor: قال الفراء : يقال أزبد الوادي إزبادا ، والزبد الاسم

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains rābiyā as floating high above the water.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r2.anchor: وقوله : { رابيا } قال الزجاج : طافيا عاليا فوق الماء

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r3.speaker: غيره
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r3.claim: Another explanation takes rābiyā as swelling or increasing, from rabā, ‘to grow.’
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r3.anchor: وقال غيره : زائدا بسبب انتفاخه ، يقال : ربا يربو إذا زاد

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r4.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read the verb in third person; Abū ʿUbayda prefers this because the next phrase says ‘benefits people’ and there is no addressee here.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم { يوقدون } بالياء ، واختاره أبو عبيدة لقوله : { ينفع الناس }

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r5.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r5.claim: The other readers use the second-person form; one possible address is the people mentioned in 13:16.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r5.anchor: والباقون بالتاء على الخطاب ، وعلى هذا التقدير ففيه وجهان . الأول : أنه خطاب للمذكورين

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r6.claim: With the second-person reading, the address may instead be general, as if speaking to all who kindle things in fire.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r6.anchor: والثاني : أنه يجوز أن يكون خطابا عاما يراد به الكافة ، كأنه قال : ومما توقدون عليه في النار

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r7.claim: Kindling upon an object can mean heating something that is not itself placed in the fire, as in Pharaoh’s instruction to Hāmān.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r7.anchor: الإيقاد على الشيء على قسمين : أحدهما : أن لا يكون ذلك الشيء في النار

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r8.claim: It can also mean putting the object itself into the fire, as when metals are melted.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r8.anchor: والثاني : أن يوقد على الشيء ويكون ذلك الشيء في النار فإن من أراد تذويب الأجساد السبعة

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r9.speaker: أهل المعاني
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r9.claim: The people of meaning say gold and silver are heated for jewelry, while iron, copper, lead, and tin are worked into utensils and other useful articles; matāʿ means anything enjoyed or used.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r9.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : الذي يوقد عليه لابتغاء حلية الذهب والفضة ، والذي يوقد عليه لابتغاء الأمتعة الحديد والنحاس والرصاص

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r10.claim: The metalworking produces foam like the foam carried by floodwater.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r10.anchor: زبد مثله } أي زبد مثل زبد الماء الذي يحمله السيل

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r11.claim: The phrase means that God sets out likenesses for truth and falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r11.anchor: المعنى كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال للحق والباطل

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r12.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses jafāʾ as casting away or throwing aside; it can name the collected, compacted mass of debris.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r12.anchor: قال الفراء : الجفاء الرمي والاطراح يقال : جفا الوادي غثاءه يجفوه جفاء إذا رماه

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r13.claim: Jafāʾ is accusative as a circumstantial expression describing the foam’s state as it is cast away.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r13.anchor: والجفاء اسم للمجتمع منه المنضم بعضه إلى بعض وموضع جفاء نصب على الحال

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r14.claim: Foam may swell and seem dominant but ultimately disappears, leaving pure water or metal; likewise, doubts and fancies eventually fade and truth remains clear of them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r14.anchor: فكذلك الشبهات والخيالات قد تقوى وتعظم إلا أنها بالآخرة تبطل وتضمحل وتزول ويبقى الحق ظاهرا لا يشوبه شيء من الشبهات

RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r15.speaker: أبو حاتم
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r15.claim: Rūʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj is reported to read jafālan; Abū Ḥātim says not to follow his reading because he ate mice.
RAZI-FULL:v19p29#2/r15.anchor: وفي قراءة رؤبة بن العجاج جفالا ، وعن أبي حاتم لا يقرأ بقراءة رؤبة لأنه كان يأكل الفار
